definition_zh: 运动；移动；动作；社会运动；乐章；走势；调动；排便
definition_en: an act of changing position or place, or an organized group working for a shared aim, or a section of a musical work
core_image: 一队人举着同样的牌子从广场一端走到另一端，脚步连成一道推进的横线
scene: 广场上，人们举着同样的牌子从一端走向另一端，队伍越来越长，喊声连成一片。The movement began with a few students and soon filled the square.
sceneCN: 这里 movement 指有共同诉求的群体性运动（第 3 个义项：社会运动）；句意：这场运动从几名学生开始，很快站满了广场。图中可辨识物件：手写标语牌、扩音器、横幅、统一的袖标；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Change of position
senses.definition: the act or process of changing position or place
senses.definitionCN: 改变位置或处所的动作或过程
senses.example: A slow movement of the shelf warned that the wall was settling.
senses.exampleCN: 架子缓缓移位，说明墙体在下沉。
senses.why: Movement is the native noun of the verb move, and its oldest sense is simply the fact of changing place.
senses.whyCN: movement 是动词 move 的本族名词，最古老的意思就是「换了地方」这件事。

senses.title: A single action of the body
senses.definition: one deliberate action or gesture, especially of the hand or body
senses.definitionCN: 一次有意的动作或姿态，尤指手或身体的
senses.example: With one movement she folded the letter and sealed it.
senses.exampleCN: 她一个动作就把信折好封上了。
senses.why: A process can be cut into single acts, and one of those acts is also called a movement.
senses.whyCN: 一个过程可以切成一个个单独的动作，其中一次也叫 movement。

senses.title: An organized campaign for a cause
senses.titleCN: 为某一诉求组织起来的社会运动
senses.definition: a group of people acting together over time to bring about a change in society or policy
senses.definitionCN: 一群人长期共同行动，以求改变社会或政策
senses.example: The movement for clean rivers spread from one town to the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 洁净河流的运动从一个镇扩展到整个河谷。
senses.why: In the nineteenth century people acting together were seen as one body on the move, so a campaign became a movement.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪，人们把共同行动的一群人看作一个在移动的整体，于是运动便成了一项社会运动。

senses.title: A section of a musical work
senses.titleCN: 长篇乐曲中的一个乐章
senses.definition: a self-contained part of a long musical composition, such as a symphony
senses.definitionCN: 长篇乐曲（如交响曲）中相对独立的一部分
senses.example: The second movement is slow and almost silent.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章缓慢而近乎无声。
senses.why: Music was thought of as advancing in stages; each stage is a movement within the whole work.
senses.whyCN: 人们把音乐想成一段段向前推进；每一个阶段就是整部作品里的一个乐章。

senses.title: A trend in figures or opinion
senses.definition: a change in level, price or opinion over time, seen as a direction
senses.definitionCN: 水平、价格或舆论随时间的变化，被看作一个方向
senses.example: The upward movement in rents began before the new bridge opened.
senses.exampleCN: 租金的上涨走势在新桥通车前就开始了。
senses.why: A line on a chart that keeps going one way looks like something travelling, so a trend is called a movement.
senses.whyCN: 图表上一直朝一个方向走的线，看起来像有东西在行进，因此趋势也被称为 movement。

senses.title: The mechanism inside a clock
senses.definition: the assembly of moving parts that drives a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 驱动钟表的整套运动部件
senses.example: The watch has a hand-wound movement and a glass back.
senses.exampleCN: 这块表是手上链机芯，背面是玻璃的。
senses.why: Watchmakers named the works by the movement they produce, and the term became the trade word for the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 钟表匠以它产生的运动来命名这套机构，这个说法后来成了整个机芯的行业词。

senses.title: A relocation of troops or supplies
senses.definition: the organized moving of troops, ships or supplies from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地把部队、船只或物资从一处移到另一处
senses.example: Satellite images tracked the movement of trucks along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星图像追踪了卡车沿边境的调动。
senses.why: A body of men or goods changing place is still the plain sense, made formal by military use.
senses.whyCN: 一批人或货物换地方，仍是那个直白的意思，只是被军事用法正式化了。

senses.title: A bowel movement
senses.definition: an act of emptying the bowels, used as a neutral medical term
senses.definitionCN: 排空肠道的一次动作，用作中性的医学说法
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's movements after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录了病人术后的排便情况。
senses.why: Medicine needed a plain, polite noun for a bodily action, and the ordinary word for moving served.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个平实而礼貌的词来指这一身体动作，于是用了「移动」这个普通词。

intro.en: Movement comes through Old French movement from movoir, the French form of Latin movere 'to move'. The musical and social senses are later growths from the plain idea of something advancing.
intro.cn: movement 经古法语 movement 来自 movoir，即拉丁 movere「移动」的法语形式。乐章义与社会运动义都是后来的引申，源自「某物在向前推进」这一朴素想法。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to set going, and it is the source of the whole French and English family.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动，是整个法语与英语词族的源头。

items.en: The French verb movoir or moveir meant to move and gave English the verb move.
items.cn: 法语动词 movoir 或 moveir 意为移动，并给英语带来了动词 move。

items.en: The noun movement named the act of moving; it uses the same action-noun ending as many French words in -ment.
items.cn: 名词 movement 指移动这一动作；它用的动作名词词尾，与许多以 -ment 结尾的法语词相同。

items.en: English took the noun in the fourteenth century, at first for physical movement and later for a single action.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个名词，起初指物理移动，后来也指单次动作。

items.en: From the eighteenth century a movement named a section of a symphony or sonata, following the idea of music advancing by stages.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，movement 指交响曲或奏鸣曲中的一个部分，沿用「音乐分段推进」的想法。

items.en: The collective sense for a campaign is a nineteenth-century growth, when large groups acting for a cause were described as one moving body.
items.cn: 指社会运动的集体义是十九世纪长出的，当时为某一诉求行动的大群人是被当作一个移动的整体来描述。

note.en: The first group shares the verb move and is often mistaken for the noun; the second group separates movement from motion, campaign and trend.
note.cn: 第一组共享动词 move，常与这个名词混淆；第二组把 movement 与 motion、campaign、trend 等词区分开。

entries.definition: The verb and a countable noun for one act of moving; movement is the noun of the process or the campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，也可数名词指一次移动；movement 指过程或社会运动。

entries.definition: Move plus -able: able to be moved, said of furniture or a feast day; it is an adjective, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表「能够」的词尾构成：可被移动的，用于家具或不固定的节期；是形容词，不是动作。

entries.definition: Move plus -ing: either in the act of moving or able to stir the feelings, as a moving speech does.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表进行或性质的词尾构成：或指正在移动，或指能打动人心，如感人的演讲。

entries.definition: A shortened form of moving picture, from the moving images on film; it is a thing, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 「活动影像」一词的缩略，来自胶片上移动的影像；指作品，不是动作。

entries.definition: Move plus -er: a person or thing that moves something, or a company that transports goods.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表施动者的词尾构成：推动某事的人或物，也指搬家公司。

entries.definition: Often a single physical act or a formal proposal; movement is wider and covers campaigns and trends.
entries.definitionCN: 多指单次物理动作或正式动议；movement 范围更宽，还涵盖社会运动与趋势。

entries.definition: An organized series of actions for a goal; a movement is broader and longer, and usually social.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目标组织的一系列行动；movement 更宽、更久，通常带社会性。

entries.definition: A strong effort or campaign to reach a target, often official; it stresses the push, not the people.
entries.definitionCN: 为达目标的有力推动或活动，常是官方发起的；强调推动力，不强调人群。

entries.definition: The general direction in which something is changing; movement can name a change in figures but is more concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 事物变化的总方向；movement 也能指数字变动，但更具体。

entries.definition: The ability to move from place to place, used of animals and vehicles; it is technical and not social.
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处移动的能力，用于动物和交通工具；属技术用语，不含社会义。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for move, and movement is the noun made from the French verb.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，movement 是由法语动词变来的名词。

normal.en: The family runs move, movable, moving, movie, mover.
normal.cn: 同族词有 move、movable、moving、movie、mover。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: social movement, slow movement, upward movement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：社会运动、慢乐章、上升走势。

normal.en: The -ment ending turns an action into a noun, as in agreement and management.
normal.cn: 名词词尾把动作变成名词，如「同意」与「管理」二词。

normal.en: A clock's movement is the works that keep it moving, a trade term from watchmaking.
normal.cn: 钟表的 movement 是让它持续运转的机芯，这是制表业的行业说法。

abstract.en: Picture one person walking, then a hundred walking in the same direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走，然后一百个人朝同一个方向走。

abstract.en: Picture a symphony advancing one stage at a time, each stage its own room.
abstract.cn: 想象一部交响曲一段段向前走，每个阶段自成一间屋子。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a graph climbing and someone calling that climb a movement.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线往上爬，有人把这段爬升叫 movement。

examples.en: The movement of goods across the border slowed after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，货物过境的流动变慢了。

examples.en: The civil rights movement changed the town's hiring rules.
examples.cn: 民权运动改变了这座小镇的用工规定。

examples.en: A thermostat senses the movement of air through the duct.
examples.cn: 恒温器感知空气在管道中的流动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「move（挪）+ ment（门特）」——挪一挪，人群就成了一场运动；movement 移动、运动、乐章

root: 拉丁 movere「移动」→ 古法语 movoir「移动」→ 古法语名词 movement「移动、动作」→ 英语 movement；乐章义由乐曲内部的推进，社会运动义为十九世纪集体行动的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one body in motion: it changes place, makes a single act, gathers into a campaign, advances as a section of music, climbs as a trend, drives a clock, moves as troops, and passes as a bodily function.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「在动的身体」展开：它换位、做出一次动作、聚成一场运动、作为乐曲的一部分推进、作为趋势上升、驱动机芯、作为部队调动，最后成为一种身体功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people walking together in one direction, their steps forming an advancing line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人朝同一方向走，脚步连成一条推进的横线。

branches.en: PLAIN MOVING: one body changes place, and one deliberate action of the hand is carved out of it.
branches.cn: 直白的动：一具身体换了地方，其中切出手的一次有意动作。

branches.en: PEOPLE TOGETHER: many bodies moving for one cause become a social movement.
branches.cn: 众人同行：许多身体为一个诉求而动，聚成社会运动。

branches.en: A WORK IN STAGES: music advancing by sections gives the musical movement its name.
branches.cn: 分段推进的作品：音乐按段落向前，乐章由此得名。

branches.en: A CLIMB ON A CHART: the same advance is read as a trend in figures.
branches.cn: 图表上的爬升：同一种推进被读成数字的走势。

branches.en: MOVING PARTS AND BODIES: a watch's works, a column of trucks, and the bowels all carry the plain sense into new settings.
branches.cn: 运动部件与身体：钟表机芯、车队与肠道，都把直白义带进新的场合。

intro.en: Movement is a French action noun built on the Latin verb of moving, with the same ending that forms many English nouns.
intro.cn: movement 是一个由拉丁「移动」动词构成的法语动作名词，用的词尾也构成许多英语名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives move, motion, motive and motor; the French noun movement adds the action-noun ending to the same verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 move、motion、motive 与 motor；法语名词 movement 则在同一个动词上加动作名词词尾。

items.example: The verb supplies the push behind every sense.

items.example: The French verb passed into English as move.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词进入英语后成为 move。

items.meaning: the act of moving; a campaign
items.example: The movement began with a few students.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动从几名学生开始。

items.example: The machine's movements are smooth and silent.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器的各个动作平顺而安静。

items.meaning: to shift; to touch the feelings
items.example: Move the chair closer to the window.
The stage has a movable floor.
items.exampleCN: 这个舞台有一块可移动的地板。

items.example: It was a moving account of the flood.
items.exampleCN: 那是对洪水的感人叙述。

items.example: The movie ran for two hours.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影放映了两个小时。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀

definition_zh: 泥；烂泥；泥浆；泥料；淤泥；污名
definition_en: wet soft earth, the same material used for building, fine sediment in water and, figuratively, dirt thrown at a reputation
core_image: 雨后路上被车轮碾出的两道深沟，泥水顺着沟沿往外渗
scene: 雨下了一夜，村口的土路被车轮碾出两道深沟。The truck's wheels sank deep into the mud.
sceneCN: 这里是「泥、烂泥」（第 1 个义项：湿软的泥土）；句意为卡车的轮子深陷泥中。图中可辨识物件：土路、车辙、车轮。

pos.zh: 泥；烂泥；泥浆；泥料；淤泥；污名

collocations.zh: 泥饼（儿童用泥做的假饼）

derivatives.zh: 由 mud 加 -y 构成，义为「泥泞的」；作动词指「使浑浊」
由 mud 与 guard 复合而成，义为「挡泥板」
由 mud 与 flat 复合而成，义为「潮间带的泥滩」
由 mud 与 slinging 复合而成，义为「竞选中的抹黑攻击」

senses.title: Wet, soft earth
senses.definition: soft wet earth that sticks to shoes and wheels
senses.definitionCN: 湿软、会粘在鞋和车轮上的泥土
senses.example: The truck's wheels sank deep into the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车的轮子深陷泥中。
senses.why: The Germanic word names the soft, sticky ground itself, so the physical sensation of sticking is the centre of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个日耳曼词指的就是那种软而黏的地面本身，所以「黏住」的身体感觉是词义的中心。

senses.title: Earth and water used as building material
senses.definition: clay or earth mixed with water and shaped or spread while wet
senses.definitionCN: 黏土或泥土加水调成，趁湿塑形或涂抹的材料
senses.example: The old walls were built of mud and straw.
senses.exampleCN: 那些老墙是用泥和草茎砌成的。
senses.why: If mud is soft ground, it can also be handled and shaped, so the same word names the raw material of a wall.
senses.whyCN: 既然泥是软的地面，它也能被捧起来塑形，于是同一个词又指砌墙的原料。

senses.title: Fine sediment at the bottom of water
senses.definition: fine particles that settle on the bed of a river, lake or sea
senses.definitionCN: 沉在河、湖或海底的细小颗粒
senses.example: The river bed was covered with thick black mud.
senses.exampleCN: 河床上覆盖着厚厚的黑泥。
senses.why: Mud carried by water eventually settles, and the settled layer keeps the name of the wet earth that made it.
senses.whyCN: 被水带走的泥终究会沉下来，沉积的那一层仍沿用形成它的湿土之名。

senses.title: A reputation dirtied in public
senses.definition: used in phrases such as drag someone's name through the mud to mean public accusation and disgrace
senses.definitionCN: 用于「drag someone's name through the mud」一类说法，指公开指责与名誉受损
senses.example: The scandal dragged his name through the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 那桩丑闻把他的名声拖进泥里。
senses.why: Being covered in mud is visible and humiliating, so the image transfers neatly to a reputation covered in public accusation.
senses.whyCN: 浑身沾泥既显眼又难堪，于是这个画面很自然地转到被公开指责覆盖的名声上。

intro.en: Mud is a Germanic word for soft wet earth, probably reaching English from Low German, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: mud 是日耳曼语中表示湿软泥土的词，可能经低地德语进入英语，它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed stem often written mud- is generally thought to underlie the Germanic words for wet earth, though its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个常写作 mud- 的日耳曼语重构词干是各语言表示湿土的词的底子，但其确切形式并不确定。

items.en: Low German mudde is the form most often cited as the immediate source of the English word.
items.cn: 低地德语 mudde 是最常被引为英语这个词直接来源的形式。

items.en: Middle English mudde appeared in the thirteenth century for soft wet ground and for the mire of streets.
items.cn: 中古英语 mudde 在十三世纪出现，指湿软的地面，也指街道上的泥泞。

items.en: The spelling settled as mud, and the word spread to building material and to river sediment.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 mud，词义也扩展到建筑材料与河底沉积物。

items.en: Modern English mud keeps the literal ground sense and supplies the image behind phrases about ruined reputations.
items.cn: 现代英语的 mud 保留字面的泥土义，并为关于名誉受损的短语提供画面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the mud stem, while the near-meaning group collects other words for soft wet ground and sediment.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 mud 词干上的形式，近义组收其他表示湿软地面与沉积物的词。

entries.definition: Covered with mud, or to make something unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 沾满泥的，或使某物变得浑浊。

entries.definition: A cover that keeps mud off a wheel.
entries.definitionCN: 挡住车轮泥水的护板。

entries.definition: Low muddy ground left bare by the tide.
entries.definitionCN: 退潮后露出的低洼泥地。

entries.definition: The practice of attacking a rival's reputation in public.
entries.definitionCN: 公开攻击对手名声的做法。

entries.definition: A thin, slippery, unpleasant wet substance.
entries.definitionCN: 稀薄、湿滑而令人不适的物质。

entries.definition: Fine earth carried by water and left as sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 被水带来并沉积下来的细土。

entries.definition: Heavy, sticky earth that can be shaped when wet.
entries.definitionCN: 湿时可塑形的厚重黏土。

entries.definition: Thick, soft, dirty material, often industrial waste.
entries.definitionCN: 浓稠、柔软而肮脏的物质，常指工业废泥。

normalIntro.en: The word names the soft ground itself, and its family keeps adding things to it or moving it with water.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指的就是那种软的地面本身，同族词则不断给它加东西，或让它随水流动。

normal.en: Mud probably came into English from Low German mudde, which is why its shape is so short and plain.
normal.cn: mud 很可能从低地德语 mudde 进入英语，所以它的词形才如此短而朴素。

normal.en: muddy adds -y to mud: full of mud, therefore unclear and stained.
normal.cn: muddy 在 mud 后加 -y，意为「满是泥的」，因此也指浑浊与沾污。

normal.en: mudguard and mudflat are compounds: one stops mud, the other names ground the tide leaves bare.
normal.cn: mudguard 与 mudflat 都是复合词：一个挡住泥，一个指潮水退后露出的泥地。

normal.en: Mud is uncountable, so one says a lot of mud rather than many muds.
normal.cn: mud 不可数，所以说 a lot of mud，而不说 many muds。

normal.en: The phrase drag a name through the mud turns the visible stain of earth into a public stain on honour.
normal.cn: 「drag a name through the mud」这个说法把泥土可见的污迹变成名誉上公开的污点。

abstract.en: Mud is what water does to solid ground when it stays too long.
abstract.cn: 泥是水在实地上停留太久之后做出来的东西。

abstract.en: Every footprint is mud remembering the shape of a shoe for a little while.
abstract.cn: 每个脚印都是泥暂时记住一只鞋的形状。

abstract.en: The same stuff that builds a wall can also dirty a name.
abstract.cn: 砌得起墙的东西，也能弄脏一个名字。

examples.en: The truck's wheels sank deep into the mud.
examples.cn: 卡车的轮子深陷泥中。

examples.en: Rain turned the path into a river of mud.
examples.cn: 雨水把小路变成了一条泥河。

examples.en: The children built castles out of mud.
examples.cn: 孩子们用泥堆起了城堡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马的」——马的在泥里踩出一串深坑；记住 mud 是泥。

root: 中古英语 mudde 可能来自低地德语 mudde，指湿软的泥土；一般认为与日耳曼语表示湿土的词干有关，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is wet soft earth; the senses then divide into building material, river sediment, and the figurative stain on a reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是湿软的泥土；义项由此分出建筑材料、河底沉积物，以及名誉上的比喻性污迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two deep wheel ruts in a village road after a night of rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：下了一夜雨，村口土路上被车轮碾出的两道深辙。

branches.en: boots pulling free of a wet path
branches.cn: 靴子从湿路上拔出来

branches.en: hands shaping a wall from wet earth
branches.cn: 用手把湿土糊成墙

branches.en: a river bed layered with dark silt
branches.cn: 河床积着黑色的淤泥

branches.en: a headline that soils a reputation
branches.cn: 一条把名声弄脏的标题

branches.en: mud on a shoe and mud on a name
branches.cn: 鞋上的泥与名声上的泥

intro.en: The word is a short Germanic noun of wet earth, with an adjective ending and several compounds built on top of it.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示湿土的短名词，在它上面还长出一个形容词词尾和几个复合形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，因此拉丁语部分留空。

definition_zh: 多语的；使用多种语言的；多种语言并存的
definition_en: using or involving several languages, or able to speak several languages
core_image: 一块立在中转站的分区指示牌，同一行信息用四五种文字并排写出，行人抬头寻找自己的那一行
scene: 中转站的走廊上立着一块分区指示牌，同一行信息用四五种文字并排写出。A multilingual notice board greeted arrivals in every language spoken along the route.
sceneCN: 这里指「同时使用多种语言的」（第 1 个义项：涉及多种语言并用）；句意为一块多语告示牌用沿线路途所讲的每种语言迎接抵达者。可辨识物件：指示牌、多行文字、走廊、行人。

pos.zh: 多语的；使用多种语言的
使用多种语言的人（较少用）

derivatives.zh: 多语现象；多语能力
以多语方式
语言
双语的
单语的

senses.title: Using several languages
senses.definition: describing a person, group or thing that works in more than two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述在两种以上语言中运作的人、群体或事物
senses.example: The reception desk is multilingual and answers in four tongues.
senses.exampleCN: 前台是多语的，能用四种语言应答。
senses.why: the word joins a prefix for 'many' to the root for language, so it simply counts tongues.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表「许多」的前缀与表「语言」的词根相连，因此它只是数语言的数目。

senses.title: A society with many languages
senses.definition: describing a community in which several languages are in daily use
senses.definitionCN: 描述若干语言在日常中同时使用的社群
senses.example: A multilingual city can hold five languages in one market.
senses.exampleCN: 一座多语城市可以在一个市场里容纳五种语言。
senses.why: a city that keeps several tongues in daily use is the plural of a bilingual town, so the same adjective covers it.
senses.whyCN: 一座日常使用几种语言的城市，是双语城镇的复数形态，同一形容词自然覆盖。

senses.title: A text or sign in several languages
senses.titleCN: 用多种语言写成的文本或标牌
senses.definition: written or printed in more than two languages at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时以两种以上语言书写或印刷
senses.example: The airport's multilingual signs were redesigned after the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 调查之后，机场的多语标牌重新设计过。
senses.why: the count becomes visible when the same words are printed side by side.
senses.whyCN: 当同一段话并排印出时，那个数目就变得可见。

senses.title: Multilingual education
senses.definition: schooling that uses several languages as media of instruction
senses.definitionCN: 以多种语言作为教学语言的教育
senses.example: Multilingual education let children begin in the language of home.
senses.exampleCN: 多语教育让孩子从家里的语言开始学。
senses.why: a school that teaches through several tongues makes the count a policy.
senses.whyCN: 用几种语言教学的学校，把这个数目变成了政策。

senses.title: Multilingual software
senses.definition: describing a program or platform that handles several languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述能处理多种语言的程序或平台
senses.example: The multilingual platform switched language with one click.
senses.exampleCN: 这个多语平台一键就能切换语言。
senses.why: software can hold several language packs, so the old adjective was extended to code.
senses.whyCN: 软件可以装几套语言包，这个旧形容词因此被扩展到代码。

senses.title: Multilingual processing in the mind
senses.definition: describing research on how a mind stores and switches among several languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述对心智如何储存并切换多种语言的研究
senses.example: Multilingual speakers activate both lexicons at once.
senses.exampleCN: 多语说话者会同时激活两套词库。
senses.why: researchers ask whether the languages compete or cooperate, and the adjective names the case.
senses.whyCN: 研究者追问这些语言是竞争还是协作，这个形容词就指这种情形。

senses.title: A multilingual workplace
senses.definition: describing an organization whose staff routinely work across languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述员工日常跨语言工作的组织
senses.example: The hospital runs a multilingual helpline for new arrivals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院为新到者开设多语求助热线。
senses.why: staff who answer in several tongues turn the adjective into a job requirement.
senses.whyCN: 用几种语言应答的员工，把这个形容词变成一项岗位要求。

senses.title: Multilingual resources
senses.definition: describing dictionaries, corpora or services provided in several languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述以多种语言提供的词典、语料或服务
senses.example: The archive released multilingual finding aids.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆发布了多语检索工具。
senses.why: once records and tools multiply languages, the word describes the shelf rather than the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 当记录与工具成倍增加语言，这个词便描述书架而非说话者。

intro.en: Multilingual joins multi- 'many', from Latin multus, to Latin lingua 'tongue, language' and the adjective ending -al. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词把表「许多」的前缀与拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」及形容词词尾相连；该前缀出自拉丁 multus。年代均为约数。

items.en: Multus meant 'much, many'. Its comparative and related forms also gave English multi- as a combining element.
items.cn: multus 意为「多的、许多的」，其比较级与相关形式也为英语提供了表「多」的组合成分。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and 'language'; its deeper origin is unsettled and no older attested form is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」；其更深来源无定论，也没有公认的更早书证形式。

items.en: The ending -alis built relational adjectives in Latin, and English -al does the same work.
items.cn: 拉丁语用形容词词尾构成关系形容词，英语的对应词尾承担同样的功能。

items.en: English formed the adjective in the nineteenth century, when travel, trade and empire made many-language contact ordinary.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪构成这个形容词，当时旅行、贸易与帝国使多语接触成为常态。

items.en: The late twentieth century applied it to software, education policy and brain research.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，它被用于软件、教育政策与脑研究。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first printed use of the English adjective is not precisely dated, and the pre-Latin root remains unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个英语形容词最早的印刷使用年代不明，其在拉丁语之前的词根亦未知。

note.en: Group one holds the numbering words for how many languages are used; group two holds terms about language arrangements.
note.cn: 第一组是按语言数量编号的词；第二组是关于语言安排的术语。

entries.definition: Using exactly two languages; multilingual means more than two and often leaves the count open.
entries.definitionCN: 指正好使用两种语言；多语则指多于两种，且常不限定具体数目。

entries.definition: Using a single language; it is the opposite pole and often appears in research contrasts.
entries.definitionCN: 指只使用一种语言，是相反的一极，常用于研究对照。

entries.definition: The state or practice of using many languages; the adjective describes what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 指多语并存的状态或实践；形容词则描述名词所指的情形。

entries.definition: A person who speaks many languages, or an adjective for such a person; it stresses personal skill.
entries.definitionCN: 指会说多种语言的人，或描述此人的形容词，强调个人能力。

entries.definition: Relating to several cultures; a society can be multicultural while sharing one language.
entries.definitionCN: 指涉及多种文化；一个社会可以共享一种语言而同时是多文化的。

entries.definition: A term favoured in European policy for a person's partial skills across several languages.
entries.definitionCN: 欧洲政策偏好的说法，指个人在多种语言上各自不完整的技能。

entries.definition: The rules a state adopts about which languages it will use; the adjective alone does not imply policy.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家对使用哪些语言所作的规定；单用形容词并不含政策义。

entries.definition: The act of turning text from one language into another; multilingual describes the result, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指把文本从一种语言转为另一种；多语描述结果，而非动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first element means many, the second means tongue, so the word counts languages.
normal.cn: 第一个成分意为「多」，第二个意为「舌头」，因此这个词是在数语言。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach it to institutions: multilingual society, education, staff.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它挂到机构上：多语社会、多语教育、多语员工。

normal.en: It stands above bilingual in a simple ladder: one, two, many.
normal.cn: 它在简单的阶梯上高于「双语的」：单语、双语、多语。

normal.en: The family runs multilingualism, multilingually, bilingual, monolingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「多语现象」「以多语方式」「双语的」「单语的」。

normal.en: A station sign with several scripts is the clearest picture of the word.
normal.cn: 写着几种文字的车站标牌，是这个词最清楚的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a single corridor where every passenger hears a different welcome.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每位乘客都听到不同的欢迎语。

abstract.en: Picture five doors into one room, each opened by a different key.
abstract.cn: 想象通向同一房间的五道门，每道由不同的钥匙打开。

abstract.en: Picture a brain holding several maps of the same city.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头脑里装着同一座城市的几张地图。

examples.en: The region has been multilingual for centuries, not only since tourism.
examples.cn: 这个地区几百年来一直多语并存，并非只因旅游业才如此。

examples.en: Multilingual ballots are required wherever literacy is uneven.
examples.cn: 在识字程度不均的地方，须提供多语选票。

examples.en: A multilingual corpus makes it possible to compare idioms across languages.
examples.cn: 多语语料库使跨语言比较习语成为可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马提林圭尔」——马背上驮着许多种语言一路走，这就是多语的。

root: 表「许多」的前缀出自拉丁 multus「多的」，后接拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」与形容词词尾；十九世纪英语构成该形容词，指使用或涉及多种语言。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses take one count and spread it across persons, cities, signs, schools, software, minds, workplaces and archives.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项拿同一个数目向外铺开：人、城市、标牌、学校、软件、心智、工作场所与档案馆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sign board whose every line appears in four or five scripts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块指示牌，每一行都用四五种文字并排写出。

branches.en: THE COUNT AND THE MIND: more than two languages, held and used by one person.
branches.cn: 数目与心智：多于两种语言，由一个人持有并使用。

branches.en: A PLACE: cities and regions can hold several languages at once.
branches.cn: 一个地方：城市与地区可以同时容纳几种语言。

branches.en: A SURFACE: signs and documents show the count where everyone can see it.
branches.cn: 一个表面：标牌与文书把这个数目摆到人人可见之处。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: schools teach in several tongues, and workplaces answer in several.
branches.cn: 机构：学校用几种语言教学，工作场所用几种语言应答。

branches.en: TOOLS AND RECORDS: software and archives multiply the languages they carry.
branches.cn: 工具与记录：软件与档案馆成倍扩大其承载的语言。

intro.en: The word is a prefix plus a Latin root plus an adjective ending, and each part also builds a family.
intro.cn: 这个词由前缀、拉丁词根与形容词词尾构成，每一部分也都构成一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus supplies the counting prefix, Latin lingua the language root; English -al mirrors the Latin adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 multus 提供表数量的前缀，拉丁 lingua 提供「语言」词根；英语词尾对应拉丁形容词词尾。

items.example: The prefix answers the question how many.
The root names what is counted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被计数的东西。

items.example: The ending turns the count into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把数目变成描述。
这个办公室保存多语记录。

items.example: Multilingualism is normal in border towns.
items.exampleCN: 在边境城镇，多语并存是常态。

items.example: Bilingual staff covered the night desk.
Monolingual forms excluded half the residents.
items.exampleCN: 单语表格把一半居民排除在外。

definition_zh: 多个的；不止一个的；多种的；倍数
definition_en: made up of more than one part, person or element; involving several different kinds; and, as a noun, a number that another number contains an exact number of times
core_image: 同一盏灯被几面镜子映出一排一模一样的光点，一个光源变成许多个
scene: 地下车库里并排划出许多相同的车位，墙面刷着重复的编号，管理方说这是为了方便不同楼层的住户。The new block has multiple entrances so that people can reach the shops from several sides.
sceneCN: 这里是「多个的、不止一个的」（第 1 个义项：由不止一个部分或个体构成）；句意为这栋新楼开了好几个入口，人们可以从不同方向走到商店。图中可辨识物件：重复的编号、并排的车位、几处入口。

pos.zh: 多个的；不止一个的；多种的

derivatives.zh: 由 multiple 的词干加 -ply（折）构成，义为「乘；成倍增加」
由 multiply 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「乘法；增多」
由拉丁语 multus（多）加 -tude 构成，义为「大量；众多」
由前缀 multi-（多）与 cultural 复合而成，义为「多元文化的」

senses.title: Consisting of more than one part or person
senses.definition: made up of more than one person, thing or part, rather than a single one
senses.definitionCN: 由不止一个人、事物或部分构成，而不是只有一个
senses.example: The patient was given multiple tests before the diagnosis.
senses.exampleCN: 在确诊之前，病人接受了多项检查。
senses.why: Latin multus gave the first element its sense of many, and -plex says fold, so the word pictures one thing folded over several times instead of a single piece.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 multus 给这个词的前半部分带来「多」的意思，-plex 表示「折」，所以它的画面是同一件东西叠了好几层，而不是单独一份。

senses.title: Having many different kinds
senses.definition: involving several different types, causes or aspects rather than just one
senses.definitionCN: 涉及若干不同的类型、原因或方面，而不只是单一的
senses.example: The report lists multiple causes for the drop in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了销量下滑的多种原因。
senses.why: Once -plex can count the folds, it can count the kinds as well: several types laid side by side become multiple causes, a multiple problem or multiple meanings.
senses.whyCN: 既然 -plex 能数「折了几层」，它也就能数「有几种」：几种类型平铺在一起，就成了多种原因、多重问题或多重含义。

senses.title: A number contained exactly in another
senses.definition: a number that another number contains an exact number of times, as four is a multiple of two
senses.definitionCN: 能被另一个数整除的数，例如四是二的倍数
senses.example: Twelve is a multiple of three and of four.
senses.exampleCN: 十二是三和四的倍数。
senses.why: The mathematical sense keeps the picture of repeated folds: a multiple is a small unit folded over an exact number of times, with nothing left outside the count.
senses.whyCN: 数学义保留「一折再折」的画面：一个倍数就是小单位被完整地叠上若干次，一点零头都不剩。

intro.en: Multiple joins two Latin pieces, multus for many and -plex for folded, and it entered English through French as a word for what is manifold.
intro.cn: multiple 由两个拉丁成分合成：multus 意为「多」，-plex 意为「折、编织」；它经法语进入英语，指多重的东西。

items.en: Multus meant many or much and supplied the first half of a large family of counting words.
items.cn: multus 意为「多、许多」，为一大族计数词提供了前半部分。

items.en: -Plex came from plectere, to fold or weave, and it described something with a stated number of folds, as in duplex and triplex.
items.cn: -plex 出自 plectere（折、编织），描述具有特定折数的事物，如 duplex 与 triplex。

items.en: Multiplex joined the two pieces: many folds, and therefore manifold, having many parts or forms.
items.cn: multiplex 把两者合起来：许多折，因此是多样的，包含许多部分或形式。

items.en: French took multiplex as multiple and used it for what is composed of several elements rather than one.
items.cn: 法语把 multiplex 写作 multiple，用来指由若干成分而非单一成分构成的事物。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century, later making it a noun for a multiple in arithmetic and for repeated bus or train services.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，后来又把它用作名词，指算术中的倍数，也指重复开行的公交班次。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin elements for many and folds; the near-meaning group collects words for several parts and exact divisibility.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语「多」与「折」两个成分构成的词；近义组收表示若干部分与整除关系的词。

entries.definition: To increase in number, or to perform the operation of multiplication.
entries.definitionCN: 增加数量，或进行乘法运算。

entries.definition: The arithmetic operation of combining equal groups, or the act of increasing greatly.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干相等的组成合起来的算术运算，或大幅增多。

entries.definition: A very large number of people or things.
entries.definitionCN: 大量的人或事物。

entries.definition: Having two parts or two dwellings joined together; the -plex element is the same.
entries.definitionCN: 由两个部分或两所住宅相连而成；其中的 -plex 成分相同。

entries.definition: More than two but not very many.
entries.definitionCN: 多于两个但数量不大。

entries.definition: Of several different kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 好几种不同种类的。

entries.definition: Great in number; many.
entries.definitionCN: 数量很多。

entries.definition: Of many kinds or forms; also a fitting with several branches.
entries.definitionCN: 许多种类或形式的；也指多支管的接头。

normalIntro.en: The word is two Latin pieces, many plus fold, and every sense is a different way of counting repetitions.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是两个拉丁成分：多与折；每个义项都是数「重复了几次」的不同方式。

normal.en: Multus is Latin for many, so multiple starts from a plain count of more than one.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 multus 意为多，所以 multiple 的起点就是「不止一个」这个简单的计数。

normal.en: -Plex comes from folding, and duplex, triplex and multiplex all count how many folds a thing has.
normal.cn: -plex 出自「折」，duplex、triplex、multiplex 都在数一样东西折了几层。

normal.en: A multiple in arithmetic keeps that fold image: one number is folded into another an exact number of times.
normal.cn: 算术里的倍数保留了这个折叠画面：一个数被另一个数完整地叠进若干次。

normal.en: Multiply is the verb of the same family, which shows that the word is about making counts grow.
normal.cn: multiply 是同族的动词，说明这个词关心的是让数量长大。

normal.en: Multiple choice counts the options set side by side, which is why it names a test with several answers.
normal.cn: multiple choice 数的是并排摆出的几个选项，所以它指有几项答案的选择题。

abstract.en: Picture one lamp reflected in a row of mirrors, each image the same yet separately present.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被一面面镜子照出一排光点，每个映像都一样，却又各自存在。

abstract.en: A multiple is not a vague many but a countable repetition, so the word always implies a number of parts.
abstract.cn: multiple 不是笼统的「多」，而是可以数清的重复，所以它总含着「若干份」的意思。

abstract.en: When a report blames multiple causes, it says that no single cause can carry the whole story.
abstract.cn: 当报告归因于 multiple causes，它其实是在说：没有任何一个原因能独自解释全部。

examples.en: The new block has multiple entrances so that people can reach the shops from several sides.
examples.cn: 这栋新楼开了好几个入口，人们可以从不同方向走到商店。

examples.en: She checked the figures multiple times before signing the report.
examples.cn: 签字之前，她把数字核对了好几遍。

examples.en: Eight is a multiple of four.
examples.cn: 八是四的倍数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马替坡」——一匹马替几拨人爬坡，来回好几趟；记住 multiple 是多个的、多重、倍数。

root: 拉丁语 multus（多）加 -plex（折，出自 plectere 折、编织）构成 multiplex，经法语 multiple 进入英语；同族词有 multiply、multiplication、multitude、duplex 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a count of more than one; the senses divide into a number of parts, a number of kinds, and exact divisibility in arithmetic.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「不止一个」的计数；义项分出若干部分、若干种类，以及算术中的整除关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single lamp reflected in a row of mirrors, one source appearing many times.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯被一排镜子照出许多光点，一个光源重复出现。

branches.en: a doorway repeated along a wall so a crowd can spread out
branches.cn: 同一扇门在墙上重复几次，让人群分流

branches.en: one job split among several pairs of hands
branches.cn: 一件活分到好几双手上

branches.en: a list of reasons that no single cause could explain
branches.cn: 一张罗列多种原因的清单，单一原因解释不了

branches.en: a number fitting into another with nothing left over
branches.cn: 一个数正好嵌进另一个数，一点不剩

branches.en: a count that is repeated rather than merely large
branches.cn: 不是笼统地多，而是可以数清的重复

intro.en: Two Latin pieces, many and folded, plus the English words built from them hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁成分「多」与「折」，以及由它们构成的英语词，把这个词条撑了起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both halves of the word: multus for many and -plex for folds, and multiplex is the source adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了这个词的两半：multus 表示多，-plex 表示折，而 multiplex 就是来源形容词。

definition_zh: 乘；使成倍增加；增多；繁殖；增殖
definition_en: to perform multiplication, or to increase greatly in number
core_image: 两堆积木一层层往上叠，层数越高，块数翻得越快
scene: 两个孩子把积木一层层往上叠，越叠越高。If you multiply the side length by three, the area grows ninefold.
sceneCN: 这里 multiply 指「做乘法，把某个量乘上另一个量」（第 1 个义项：乘）；句意为把边长乘以三，面积就增大到九倍。图中可辨识物件：积木、两层堆叠、孩子的手、量尺；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 乘法；增殖
乘法的；倍增的
倍数；多个的
多重性；多样性
乘数；倍增因素

senses.title: To perform multiplication
senses.definition: to find the product of two or more numbers
senses.definitionCN: 求两个或更多数的乘积
senses.example: If you multiply the side length by three, the area grows ninefold.
senses.exampleCN: 把边长乘以三，面积就增大到九倍。
senses.why: multiply is the verb of folding equal copies together, and arithmetic uses it for the operation that counts those copies.
senses.whyCN: multiply 是把相同副本叠合起来的动词，算术用它来指清点这些副本的运算。

senses.title: To increase greatly
senses.definition: to make something much larger in number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物的数量或数额大大增加
senses.example: The new road multiplied the number of visitors ten times over.
senses.exampleCN: 新修的公路让访客数量增加了十倍。
senses.why: outside arithmetic the verb keeps the picture of many copies appearing: one cause produces a crowd of results.
senses.whyCN: 在算术之外，这个动词保留「许多副本出现」的画面：一个原因产生一大群结果。

senses.title: To grow in number
senses.definition: to become more numerous without an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 在没有外来施动者的情况下变得更多
senses.example: Problems multiplied while the team was away.
senses.exampleCN: 团队不在的时候，问题越来越多。
senses.why: the intransitive use shifts the focus from someone making more to things simply becoming many.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法把焦点从「有人使变多」转到「事物自己变多」。

senses.title: To breed
senses.definition: to produce offspring and so increase a population
senses.definitionCN: 产生后代，从而使种群数量增加
senses.example: The rabbits multiplied faster than the gardeners could catch them.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子繁殖得比园丁抓得还快。
senses.why: breeding is increase by copies of living things, so the old verb for increase became the verb for breeding.
senses.whyCN: 繁育就是活物靠副本增多，于是那个表示「增多」的老动词成了繁育的动词。

senses.title: For cells to divide and increase
senses.definition: to increase in number by cell division
senses.definitionCN: 通过细胞分裂而数量增多
senses.example: The cells multiply until the wound is covered.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞不断增殖，直到伤口被覆盖。
senses.why: cell division repeats copies at a microscopic scale, and the arithmetic verb describes that repetition exactly.
senses.whyCN: 细胞分裂在微观尺度上重复副本，算术里的这个动词正描述这种重复。

senses.title: To multiply out
senses.definition: to expand a product of bracketed expressions by multiplying every term
senses.definitionCN: 把括号表达式的乘积逐项相乘展开
senses.example: Multiply out the brackets before collecting like terms.
senses.exampleCN: 先把括号乘开，再合并同类项。
senses.why: the particle 'out' marks the unfolding of a folded product, the reverse of the folding image inside the word.
senses.whyCN: 「乘开」里的「开」正标出把折起的乘积展开，与词内「折叠」的形象相反。

senses.title: To multiply by a number
senses.definition: to apply a particular factor to a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 对某个量施加一个特定的倍数
senses.example: Multiply the reading by ten to get the true value.
senses.exampleCN: 把读数乘以十，就得到真实值。
senses.why: this is the everyday phrasing of the operation, with the factor named after the preposition by.
senses.whyCN: 这是这项运算的日常说法，倍数在介词之后点出来。

senses.title: To multiply one's chances
senses.definition: to make an opportunity or risk much more likely
senses.definitionCN: 使某个机会或风险的可能性大大增加
senses.example: Two applications multiplied her chances of being accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 投出两份申请，让她被录取的机会成倍增加。
senses.why: chances behave like countable copies, so making more of them feels like multiplication rather than simple addition.
senses.whyCN: 机会像可数的副本，把机会变多感觉像相乘而不是简单相加。

intro.en: Multiply comes from Latin multiplicare 'to make many-fold', from multiplex, built on multus 'many' and plicare 'to fold'. English took the verb through Old French multiplier.
intro.cn: multiply 来自拉丁 multiplicare「使成多重」，出自 multiplex，由 multus「多」与 plicare「折叠」构成。英语经古法语 multiplier 引入这个动词。

items.en: Multus meant 'many'. It also lies behind multiple, multitude and the first half of multiply.
items.cn: multus 意为「多」。它也是 multiple、multitude 以及 multiply 前半部分的来源。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold'; the same verb gives explicit 'unfolded', complicate 'folded together' and duplicate 'folded twice'.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」；同一个动词给出 explicit「展开的」、complicate「折在一起」与 duplicate「折两次」。

items.en: Multus plus -plex made multiplex 'many-fold'; the adjective pictures layers folded onto one another.
items.cn: multus 加 -plex 构成 multiplex「多重的」；这个形容词描画一层层叠在一起。

items.en: The verb multiplicare meant 'to make many-fold, increase', and arithmetic narrowed it to repeated addition.
items.cn: 动词 multiplicare 意为「使成多重、使增多」，算术把它收窄为重复相加。

items.en: Old French multiplier carried the verb into English in the thirteenth century, first as 'increase' and then as the arithmetic operation.
items.cn: 古法语 multiplier 在十三世纪把这个动词带入英语，先表示「增多」，后表示算术运算。

items.en: The first English date for the arithmetic sense is approximate; the Latin verb and its parts are securely attested.
items.cn: 算术义在英语中的最早年代为约数；这个拉丁动词及其构件则有可靠记录。

note.en: The first group shares the folding root and is easily confused; the second group names other kinds of growth.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「折叠」的词根，容易混淆；第二组是其他增长方式。

entries.definition: A number divisible by another, or an adjective meaning many; it names a result, not the act of multiplying.
entries.definitionCN: 指能被另一个数整除的数，或形容词「多个的」；命名的是结果，不是相乘的动作。

entries.definition: The noun of the operation; it names the act or the process that multiply performs.
entries.definitionCN: 这项运算的名词；命名 multiply 所执行的动作或过程。

entries.definition: The quality of being many; it counts kinds or instances rather than performing a product.
entries.definitionCN: 指「多」的性质；数的是种类或实例，不做乘积。

entries.definition: Many-fold or having many parts; it keeps the old adjective without becoming a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指多重的或有许多部分的；保留老形容词，并未变成动词。

entries.definition: From explicare 'to unfold'; it shares plicare and means fully stated, with no arithmetic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 explicare「展开」；共享 plicare，意为明确说出的，没有算术义。

entries.definition: To become larger or more; it lacks the sense of equal copies folded together.
entries.definitionCN: 指变大或变多；不含相同副本叠合的意思。

entries.definition: To increase quickly by producing new parts; it stresses spreading, not the arithmetic rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过产生新部分而迅速增多；强调扩散，而非算术规则。

entries.definition: To produce offspring; multiplying can describe the resulting rise in numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生后代；multiplying 可以描述由此带来的数量上升。

entries.definition: To grow in size or scope; it does not imply counting equal groups.
entries.definitionCN: 指规模或范围扩大；不含清点相同组的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: multus 'many' plus plicare 'fold': to fold many copies into one product.
normal.cn: multus「多」加 plicare「折」：把许多副本折成一个乘积。

normal.en: The family runs multiply, multiplication, multiple, multiplicity and multiplier.
normal.cn: 同族词有 multiply、multiplication、multiple、multiplicity 与 multiplier。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: multiply by, multiply out, multiply in number.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：乘以、乘开、数量增多。

normal.en: Multiply out is the reverse of the folding inside the word: layers come apart into terms.
normal.cn: multiply out 与词内的「折」相反：层叠散开成为一项一项。

normal.en: Rabbits are the classic example of the breeding sense: they multiply faster than anyone can count.
normal.cn: 兔子是繁殖义的经典例子：它们增多得比谁数得都快。

abstract.en: Picture one brick that becomes two, then four, then eight, in the same minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一块砖在同一分钟里变成两块、四块、八块。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour spreading from one table to every table in the hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻从一桌传到大厅里的每一桌。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of brackets opening outward like a pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一对括号像两只手一样向外张开。

examples.en: Multiply the length by the width to get the area.
examples.cn: 把长乘以宽就得到面积。

examples.en: Bacteria multiply rapidly in warm, moist conditions.
examples.cn: 细菌在温暖潮湿的条件下迅速繁殖。

examples.en: Multiply out the brackets and then simplify the result.
examples.cn: 把括号乘开，然后化简结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满多倍」——一层层叠成多倍 → 乘、成倍增多

root: 拉丁 multus「多」+ plicare「折叠」→ multiplex「多重的」→ multiplicare「使增多」→ 古法语 multiplier → 英语 multiply。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one verb of folding copies: making a product, making much more, becoming many, breeding, cells dividing, opening brackets, applying a factor and swelling one's chances.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个「把副本叠起来」的动词：求乘积、使多得多、自身变多、繁殖、细胞分裂、打开括号、施加倍数，以及把机会撑大。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two stacks of blocks folded upward, the count rising faster than the height.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堆积木层层往上叠，块数比高度涨得更快。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: finding a product, and applying a named factor to a quantity.
branches.cn: 运算：求乘积，以及对某个量施加点名的倍数。

branches.en: MAKING MORE: swelling a number greatly, and swelling someone's chances.
branches.cn: 使更多：让数量大大增加，也让机会大大增加。

branches.en: BECOMING MANY: problems and troubles simply grow in number.
branches.cn: 自己变多：问题与麻烦就这样越来越多。

branches.en: LIFE COPIES ITSELF: rabbits breeding and cells dividing are the same arithmetic in flesh.
branches.cn: 生命复制自身：兔子繁殖与细胞分裂，是同一套算术长在血肉里。

branches.en: OPEN THE BRACKETS: multiply out unfolds the product term by term.
branches.cn: 打开括号：乘开把乘积一项一项地展开。

intro.en: Multiply is a Latin verb of folding many together; its pieces and endings build a large English family.
intro.cn: multiply 是一个拉丁动词，意为把许多层折在一起；其构件与词尾构成一个很大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus and plicare give multiple, multiplex, multiplicity, explicit, complicate and duplicate; the verb ending -are became English -ify through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 multus 与 plicare 衍生 multiple、multiplex、multiplicity、explicit、complicate 与 duplicate；动词词尾 -are 经法语变成英语的 -ify。

items.example: The adjective stays in English as multiplex.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词以 multiplex 的形式留在英语里。

items.example: The Latin verb is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是直接来源。

items.meaning: to make a product; to increase
a number that contains another exactly
items.example: Six is a multiple of two.
The multiplicity of voices filled the room.

items.meaning: the number or factor that multiplies
items.exampleCN: 这个乘数把每个分数都抬高了。

items.meaningCN: 表示「使成为」的动词后缀
items.example: It also appears in simplify and amplify.
items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 simplify 与 amplify 里。

definition_zh: 谋杀；凶杀；谋杀罪；糟蹋；彻底击败
definition_en: the crime of killing a person deliberately; to kill someone unlawfully and on purpose; also, in loose use, to ruin a piece of work or defeat an opponent completely
core_image: 一只手的影子按在另一个人的影子上，把对方从地面上抹去
scene: 侦探在雨后的巷口拉起警戒线，墙角的脚印还湿着，围观的人低声说这不像意外。The detective read the report and concluded that the man had been murdered in his own kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里是「谋杀、蓄意杀害」（第 1 个义项：非法且故意地夺去他人性命）；句意为侦探看过报告后断定这名男子是在自家厨房里被杀害的。图中可辨识物件：警戒线、湿脚印、厨房门。

pos.zh: 蓄意杀害；糟蹋；彻底击败

derivatives.zh: 由 murder 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「凶手；谋杀者」
由 murder 加 -ous 构成，义为「蓄意杀人的；极其危险的」
由 murderer 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，义为「女凶手」

senses.title: The crime of killing a person on purpose
senses.definition: the crime of killing another person deliberately and unlawfully
senses.definitionCN: 非法且故意地杀害他人的罪行
senses.example: The trial lasted two weeks and ended in a verdict of murder.
senses.exampleCN: 审判持续了两周，最终裁定为谋杀。
senses.why: Old English morthor named a hidden killing, a death kept secret, so the word first recorded concealment rather than the weapon.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 morthor 指暗中进行的杀害，是「不让外人知道的死亡」，所以这个词最早记录的重点是隐秘，而不是凶器。

senses.title: To kill a person unlawfully and deliberately
senses.definition: to kill someone on purpose and against the law
senses.definitionCN: 故意且违法地夺去他人生命
senses.example: Police believe the same person murdered two shopkeepers.
senses.exampleCN: 警方认为同一个人杀害了两名店主。
senses.why: Once the noun named the hidden act, the verb could name doing it, and the law uses the pair to separate a planned killing from an accident.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然指这种隐秘的行为，动词就能指做出这种行为；法律用这一对词把有预谋的杀害与意外区分开。

senses.title: Murder as a charge in law
senses.definition: the offence itself as charged in court, carrying the heaviest penalty in many legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上被指控的罪名本身，在许多法律体系里对应最重的刑罚
senses.example: He was charged with murder and held without bail.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控谋杀，不得保释。
senses.why: Legal language turned the act into a countable charge, so murder can stand in a courtroom list beside theft and fraud.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言把这种行为变成一个可列举的罪名，于是 murder 能和盗窃、欺诈一起出现在法庭的罪名清单里。

senses.title: To ruin a performance or defeat an opponent badly
senses.definition: in informal use, to spoil a piece of work or beat an opponent by a wide margin
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中把作品弄坏，或以很大差距击败对手
senses.example: The young pianist murdered the difficult passage but never lost the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻钢琴手把那一段难弹的乐句糟蹋了，却始终没有失去听众。
senses.why: The violent core image survives in slang as exaggeration: a singer who murders a song figuratively kills it, and the same hyperbole covers a heavy defeat.
senses.whyCN: 暴力的核心意象在俚语里以夸张的方式保留下来：歌手 murder 一首歌，就是把歌「弄死」了；同样的夸张也用来形容惨败。

intro.en: Murder is one of the oldest English words for killing, and its earliest use stresses secrecy rather than the manner of death.
intro.cn: murder 是英语里最古老的表示杀害的词之一，最早的用法强调的是隐秘，而不是死亡的方式。

items.en: Morthor named a secret killing, a death that the killer tried to hide, and the word kept that shadow of concealment.
items.cn: morthor 指私下进行的杀害，是凶手想要掩盖的死亡，这个词一直保留着隐瞒的阴影。

items.en: The verb morthrian meant to commit such a killing, and noun and verb travelled together into later English.
items.cn: 动词 morthrian 意为实施这类杀害，名词和动词一起进入了后来的英语。

items.en: Middle English murdren and murdre referred to both the act and the crime, and the modern spelling settled after the noun.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 murdren 与 murdre，兼指行为和罪名，现代拼写大致在名词之后固定下来。

items.en: Norman French gave English the legal pairing for a killing done with malice, and the courts kept murder apart from manslaughter.
items.cn: 诺曼法语给英语带来了「恶意杀害」的法律搭配，法庭把 murder 与过失杀人清楚分开。

items.en: Modern English keeps the criminal sense and adds a loose everyday sense in which a bad performance or a heavy defeat is called murder.
items.cn: 现代英语保留犯罪义，又加上日常的宽松用法，把糟糕的表演或惨败也称作 murder。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family of murder plus two words that merely share its shape; the near-meaning group collects other verbs and legal terms for killing.
note.cn: 形近组收 murder 的同族词，以及两个只是字形接近的词；近义组收其他表示杀害的动词与法律术语。

entries.definition: The person who commits a murder.
entries.definitionCN: 实施谋杀的人。

entries.definition: Capable of or intending to kill; extremely dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 有杀人意图的；极其危险的。

entries.definition: To speak quietly under the breath; only the shape resembles murder, the origins differ.
entries.definitionCN: 低声咕哝；只是字形接近 murder，词源不同。

entries.definition: A soft, low sound; the spelling is close but the word has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 轻柔低沉的声音；拼写相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: To cause someone or something to die.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物死亡。

entries.definition: To kill a prominent person, usually for political reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 通常出于政治原因刺杀要人。

entries.definition: To kill, especially violently, used mostly in old or literary texts.
entries.definitionCN: 杀害，尤指暴力杀害，多用于古旧或文学作品。

entries.definition: The killing of one person by another, whether lawful or not.
entries.definitionCN: 一人致另一人死亡，无论是否合法。

normalIntro.en: One old English noun of secret killing, its verb and its legal afterlife explain both the crime and the slang.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示暗中杀害的古英语名词、它的动词，以及它在法律里的延续，同时解释了罪名与俚语。

normal.en: Old English morthor meant a secret killing, so the word begins with concealment rather than with blood.
normal.cn: 古英语 morthor 意为暗中的杀害，所以这个词起点是「隐瞒」，而不是血。

normal.en: Murderer adds -er, the person, while murderous adds -ous, the quality; both stay inside the criminal family.
normal.cn: murderer 加 -er 指人，murderous 加 -ous 指性质，两者都留在犯罪这个词族里。

normal.en: The law keeps murder, deliberate, apart from manslaughter, without intent, and the pair still defines the charge.
normal.cn: 法律把表示故意的 murder 与表示无意的 manslaughter 分开，这一对词至今界定着罪名。

normal.en: Noun and verb share one idea, so you can commit a murder or murder a person with no change of meaning.
normal.cn: 名词与动词共用一个意思，所以 commit a murder 与 murder a person 含义不变。

normal.en: The slang sense survives because murder is extreme, and exaggeration borrows extreme words for bad singing and heavy defeat.
normal.cn: 俚语义能留下来，是因为 murder 足够极端；夸张正好借极端词来形容走调的演唱和惨败。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow pressing another shadow into the ground until it disappears.
abstract.cn: 想象一个影子把另一个影子按进地面，直到它消失。

abstract.en: A word for a hidden death reminds you that concealment, not noise, was the original danger.
abstract.cn: 一个表示暗中死亡的词提醒人：最早的危险是掩盖，而不是声响。

abstract.en: Because it names an irreversible act, murder can be borrowed only loosely for a spoiled song or a lost match.
abstract.cn: 因为它指的是一种不可逆的行为，所以只能宽松地借来说糟蹋一首歌或输掉一场比赛。

examples.en: The court found that she had murdered her business partner.
examples.cn: 法庭认定她谋杀了她的生意伙伴。

examples.en: He was charged with murder after the body was found.
examples.cn: 尸体被发现后，他被控谋杀。

examples.en: Our team murdered them in the second half.
examples.cn: 我们队在下半场把他们彻底击败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抹的」——把人从世上抹掉，就是 murder；记住它是谋杀。

root: 古英语 morthor（暗中的杀害）与动词 morthrian 构成，中古英语作 murdre，诺曼法语强化了法律用法；同族词有 murderer、murderous，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a killing kept secret; the senses divide into the crime, the act, the legal charge, and a slang exaggeration.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是隐秘的杀害；义项分出罪行、行为、法律罪名，以及俚语里的夸张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shadow pressing another shadow flat against the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个影子把另一个影子按平在地面上。

branches.en: a strip of tape sealing off a dark doorway
branches.cn: 封住黑暗门洞的警戒带

branches.en: a story told to neighbours that nobody believes
branches.cn: 讲给邻居听却没人相信的说法

branches.en: a hand doing what the law forbids
branches.cn: 做了法律禁止之事的那只手

branches.en: a charge read aloud in a courtroom
branches.cn: 法庭上被宣读的一项罪名

branches.en: a song shouted off key into a microphone
branches.cn: 对着麦克风走调喊完的一首歌

intro.en: An Old English noun and verb of secret killing, two English suffixes and the modern compounds carry the entry.
intro.cn: 一个表示暗中杀害的古英语名词与动词、两个英语后缀，以及现代复合形式，撑起了这个词条。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: murder belongs to the Old English stock, and its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：murder 属于古英语词汇，其亲属词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 肌肉；肌力；体力；影响力；实力
definition_en: body tissue made of fibres that can contract and produce movement, or the strength and power that such tissue gives
core_image: 一束束能自己收紧的绳索，一收紧就把相连的骨头拉动
scene: 健身房教练让学员把手贴上上臂，感受发力时那团组织的变化： He felt the muscle tighten under his hand.
sceneCN: 这里指「一块肌肉」（第 2 个义项：作为解剖单位的一块肌肉）；句意为他把手按在上臂，感到那块肌肉绷紧；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 力量；体力；（政治、军事上的）实力

forms.label: 形容词（肌肉的；肌肉发达的）
动词（强行挤入；使劲搬动）

derivatives.zh: 肌肉的；肌肉发达的；强有力的
肌肉系统；肌群
肌肉发达的程度
