senses.title: Contractile tissue
senses.titleCN: 肌肉组织：能收缩的纤维组织
senses.definition: tissue built from fibres that shorten when stimulated and so produce movement
senses.definitionCN: 由受刺激会缩短的纤维构成、从而产生运动的组织
senses.example: Skeletal muscle is built from long fibres that shorten when a nerve signal arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 骨骼肌由长纤维构成，神经信号到达时这些纤维会缩短。
senses.why: The core of the word is not shape but action: the tissue exists to pull, and only contraction makes it useful.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心不是形状而是动作：这种组织为拉动而生，只有收缩才使它有用。

senses.title: A single muscle organ
senses.titleCN: 一块肌肉：解剖学上的独立单位
senses.definition: one named bundle of muscle tissue with its own attachments, such as the biceps
senses.definitionCN: 一束有名称、有自身附着点的肌肉组织，如肱二头肌
senses.example: The surgeon repaired the muscle that controls the shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生修复了控制肩部的那块肌肉。
senses.why: Anatomy counts bundles rather than the material, so the mass of tissue becomes a countable organ with a name.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学按束计数而不按材料计数，于是整团组织变成有名字、可计数的器官。

senses.title: Smooth muscle
senses.titleCN: 平滑肌：内脏壁上的不随意肌
senses.definition: the involuntary muscle found in the walls of blood vessels and internal organs
senses.definitionCN: 分布于血管壁与内脏壁、不受意志控制的肌肉
senses.example: Smooth muscle in the artery wall narrows the vessel and raises blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉壁的平滑肌使血管变窄，从而升高血压。
senses.why: The same contractile tissue works without orders from the will, so it is classified by where it sits and how it is controlled.
senses.whyCN: 同一种收缩组织可以不听意志指挥，因此按所在位置与控制方式另行分类。

senses.title: Cardiac muscle
senses.titleCN: 心肌：持续搏动的特化肌肉
senses.definition: the muscle of the heart wall, which contracts rhythmically without resting
senses.definitionCN: 心壁的肌肉，有节律地收缩且从不休息
senses.example: Cardiac muscle keeps beating without rest for a lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 心肌一生都在跳动，从不休息。
senses.why: Heart muscle is a special case: it is striated like skeletal muscle but works continuously and involuntarily.
senses.whyCN: 心肌是个特例：它像骨骼肌一样有横纹，却持续工作且不受意志控制。

senses.title: Physical strength
senses.definition: the strength of the body, thought of as the power its muscles supply
senses.definitionCN: 身体的力量，被看作肌肉提供的力量
senses.example: It took real muscle to move the piano up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 把钢琴搬上楼确实费了不少力气。
senses.why: Strength is what muscle does, so the tissue name is used for the force itself, much as brains can stand for intelligence.
senses.whyCN: 力量是肌肉做的事，于是组织名称被用来指这种力，就像「头脑」一词可以指智力一样。

senses.title: Influence and pressure
senses.definition: power to make things happen, especially when used to push a plan through
senses.definitionCN: 推动事情办成的力量，尤指用来推动某项计划
senses.example: The mayor put muscle behind the housing plan and forced a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 市长为住房计划施加影响，推动了表决。
senses.why: Political force is imagined as bodily force: you lean on people the way a muscle leans on a load.
senses.whyCN: 政治力量被想象成身体力量：你对人施压，正如肌肉对重物施力。

senses.title: Military or economic power
senses.titleCN: 军事或经济实力（展示实力）
senses.definition: visible national or corporate power, displayed to discourage rivals
senses.definitionCN: 为震慑对手而展示的国家或企业实力
senses.example: The country showed its military muscle in a large joint exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家通过大规模联合演习展示军事实力。
senses.why: The display is the point: the tissue is shown rather than used, and the show is meant to be seen and feared.
senses.whyCN: 展示本身就是目的：实力被亮出来而不一定真正使用，亮的目的是让人看见并忌惮。

senses.title: Muscle memory
senses.titleCN: 肌肉记忆：熟练到无需思考的动作
senses.definition: movement skills stored so deeply by practice that they feel automatic
senses.definitionCN: 经反复练习深植、几乎自动完成的动作技能
senses.example: After years of practice, the moves are stored in muscle memory.
senses.exampleCN: 多年练习之后，这些动作已存入肌肉记忆。
senses.why: The body seems to remember what the mind no longer rehearses, so the tissue is credited with the memory.
senses.whyCN: 身体似乎记住了头脑不再预演的东西，于是这份记忆被归到肌肉名下。

intro.en: Muscle goes back to Latin musculus, literally little mouse, a diminutive of mus mouse. The image is usually explained as a moving bulge under the skin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: muscle 可追溯到拉丁语 musculus，字面义「小老鼠」，是 mus「老鼠」的指小形式。一般认为这个形象来自皮下随动作鼓动的一块。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin musculus meant both a little mouse and a muscle. Roman writers already used it for the fleshy moving parts of the body.
items.cn: 拉丁 musculus 既指「小老鼠」，也指「肌肉」。罗马作家已用它指身体中会鼓动的肉。

items.en: The common explanation is that a muscle moving under the skin looked like a mouse running beneath cloth. This is generally accepted as an image, but it is a popular explanation rather than a documented ancient statement.
items.cn: 通常的解释是：皮下活动的肌肉像一只在布下跑动的老鼠。这一形象一般被认为是来源，但它属于通行解释，并非有明文记载的古人说明。

items.en: Greek mys meant both mouse and muscle, showing that the double meaning is very old and not a Latin invention.
items.cn: 希腊语 mys 同时指老鼠与肌肉，说明这种双重含义非常古老，并非拉丁语的独创。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as PIE mus-, seen in several branches of the family; the form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 其祖词被重构为原始印欧语 mus-，见于语系的多个分支；这一形式是重构形式，并非有书证的词。

items.en: Old French muscle carried the anatomical sense into English in the fourteenth century. The spelling kept the Latin -culus stem but dropped the ending.
items.cn: 古法语 muscle 在 14 世纪把解剖义带入英语。拼写保留了拉丁词干 -culus，但去掉了词尾。

items.en: The division into skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle belongs to seventeenth- to nineteenth-century physiology; the exact dates of each label are uncertain.
items.cn: 把肌肉分为骨骼肌、平滑肌与心肌，属于 17 至 19 世纪的生理学工作；各名称的准确年代已难确考。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound like muscle; the second holds body parts and strength words that are often used in its place.
note.cn: 第一组是与 muscle 形近或音近的词；第二组是常被用来替代它的身体部位词与力量词。

entries.definition: A sea shellfish with a dark shell. It sounds exactly like muscle but has no anatomical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 一种深色贝壳的海产贝类。读音与 muscle 完全相同，但没有解剖义。

entries.definition: The snout of an animal, or a device fitted over it; the ending is -le after a z sound, not -cle.
entries.definitionCN: 动物的口鼻部，或套在其上的装置；结尾是 z 音后的 -le，而不是 -cle。

entries.definition: The adjective of muscle, meaning relating to muscle or well developed; it cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: muscle 的形容词，意为「肌肉的」或「肌肉发达的」，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: The whole system of muscles in a body or a region, not one single muscle.
entries.definitionCN: 一个身体或一个部位的全部肌肉系统，而非单独一块肌肉。

entries.definition: A strong cord that attaches muscle to bone; it carries the pull but cannot contract itself.
entries.definitionCN: 把肌肉连到骨的强韧索带；它传递拉力，但自身不能收缩。

entries.definition: A band that holds bone to bone and stabilises a joint; it does not generate movement.
entries.definitionCN: 把骨与骨系住、稳定关节的带状结构；它不产生运动。

entries.definition: An older English word for a tendon, and figuratively for strength; muscle is the flesh that pulls it.
entries.definitionCN: 指肌腱的古老英语词，也可比喻力量；肌肉则是拉动它的那团肉。

entries.definition: Muscular strength, especially of a heavy build; it names the power rather than the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指魁梧体格带来的肌肉力量；它指力量而非器官。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin diminutive, the real Greek double meaning, and real medical compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁指小形式、真实的希腊语双重含义，以及真实的医学术语组合。

normal.en: Latin musculus is a diminutive of mus mouse, and Greek mys has the same double meaning of mouse and muscle.
normal.cn: 拉丁 musculus 是 mus「老鼠」的指小形式，希腊 mys 也有老鼠与肌肉的双重含义。

normal.en: The adjective is muscular and the collective noun is musculature; neither is a plural of muscle.
normal.cn: 形容词是 muscular，集合名词是 musculature；两者都不是 muscle 的复数。

normal.en: Skeletal muscle is voluntary, smooth muscle is involuntary, cardiac muscle is involuntary and rhythmic.
normal.cn: 骨骼肌受意志控制，平滑肌不受控制，心肌不受控制而有节律。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the meanings: muscle mass and muscle fiber are tissue; muscle memory and show muscle are figurative.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分了词义：muscle mass 与 muscle fiber 指组织；muscle memory 与 show muscle 是比喻。

normal.en: The same tissue is called brawn when the point is strength and sinew when the point is the cord.
normal.cn: 当重点在力量时同一组织被称为 brawn，当重点在索带时则称 sinew。

abstract.en: Picture a rope that shortens by itself, and the bone tied to it must follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一根会自己缩短的绳子，被它系住的骨头只能跟着动。

abstract.en: Picture a small animal moving under a cloth: that is the old image behind the Latin name.
abstract.cn: 想象布下有一只小动物在移动：这正是那个拉丁名称背后的古老形象。

abstract.en: Picture influence as a hand pressing on a door: political muscle is the same gesture without a body.
abstract.cn: 想象影响力是一只压住门的手：政治实力就是同一个动作，只是不再有身体。

examples.en: Regular training increases both muscle mass and muscle strength.
examples.cn: 规律训练既能增加肌肉量，也能提高肌力。

examples.en: The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle that drives every breath.
examples.cn: 膈是一层肌肉，驱动每一次呼吸。

examples.en: The company flexed its financial muscle to buy out its rival.
examples.cn: 这家公司展示财力，收购了对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马搜」（muscle）——马拉车靠的是一束束能收紧的绳索 → 肌肉

root: 拉丁 musculus「小老鼠」，为 mus「老鼠」的指小形式；一般认为皮下鼓动的肌肉被比作布下跑动的老鼠。希腊语 mys 兼指老鼠与肌肉，祖词为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one action: fibres shorten and pull. The action is then named as tissue, as a single organ, as three tissue types, as bodily force, as social pressure, as national power, and finally as memory stored in movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在一个动作上：纤维缩短并拉动。这个动作依次被命名为组织、单块器官、三种组织类型、身体力量、社会压力、国家实力，最后是储存在动作里的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bundles of rope that shorten on command and drag whatever they are tied to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束束听令缩短的绳索，把系住的东西拖着走。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND UNIT: the tissue as material, and one named bundle as an organ.
branches.cn: 材料与单位：作为材料的组织，以及作为器官的一块有名称的肌束。

branches.en: CONTROL TYPES: smooth muscle works unseen, cardiac muscle works without pause.
branches.cn: 控制类型：平滑肌在暗处工作，心肌不停歇地工作。

branches.en: SKILL AND FORCE: strength that moves a piano, and skill that moves without thought.
branches.cn: 力量与技能：能搬动钢琴的力气，以及不经思考就能完成的技能。

branches.en: SHOWN POWER: strength displayed to deter rivals.
branches.cn: 向外展示的力量：为震慑对手而摆出的实力。

branches.en: The bridge between body and politics: the same verb put muscle behind works for both.
branches.cn: 身体与政治的桥梁：同一个搭配 put muscle behind 对两者都适用。

intro.en: Muscle is a Latin diminutive, so its ending -culus is a suffix of smallness rather than a meaningful root; the modern family grows from the stem muscul-.
intro.cn: muscle 是拉丁指小词，结尾 -culus 是表示「小」的后缀而非有实义的词根；现代词族由词干 muscul- 生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin musculus and its root mus give the English family muscular, musculature and muscularity; the Greek doublet mys explains why the same image appears in both languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musculus 及其词根 mus 衍生英语的 muscular、musculature、muscularity；希腊语中的对应词 mys 说明两种语言为何出现同一形象。

items.example: The root is the ordinary Latin word for a mouse.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是拉丁语中表示老鼠的普通名词。

items.example: Musculus is literally a little mouse.
Latin anatomy named the moving flesh musculus.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁解剖学把会鼓动的肉称为 musculus。

items.example: Muscular tissue responds to nerve signals.
items.exampleCN: 肌肉组织对神经信号作出反应。

items.example: The athlete has a powerful musculature.
items.exampleCN: 这名运动员肌肉系统强健。

items.example: Judges score muscularity as well as leanness.
items.exampleCN: 裁判既看精瘦程度，也看肌肉发达程度。

items.meaning: a heavily built man, often hired as a guard or thug
items.meaningCN: 体格魁梧的男子，常受雇充当打手
items.example: Two musclemen stood at the door.

items.meaning: relating to the link between nerves and muscles
items.meaningCN: 与神经和肌肉连接有关的
items.example: The neuromuscular junction passes the signal across.
items.exampleCN: 神经肌肉接头把信号传递过去。

items.meaning: inside a muscle, as an injection
items.meaningCN: 肌肉内部的，如肌肉注射
items.example: The vaccine was given by an intramuscular injection.
items.exampleCN: 疫苗通过肌肉注射给药。

definition_zh: 博物馆；陈列馆；馆藏机构；专门展室
definition_en: a building where objects of artistic, historical or scientific interest are collected, studied and shown to the public, and also the institution or collection itself
core_image: 玻璃柜里一排旧陶罐，被一盏小灯照出细密的裂纹
scene: 展厅里灯光压得很低，孩子们贴着玻璃柜找一只陶罐上的裂缝，讲解员说它在地下埋了很久。The city museum keeps a whole floor of pottery that was found beneath the old market.
sceneCN: 这里是「博物馆」（第 1 个义项：收藏并陈列文物或艺术品的场所）；句意为这座市立博物馆留出整整一层，陈列旧市场地下挖出的陶器。图中可辨识物件：玻璃柜、陶罐、射灯。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 mousa（缪斯）与 -logy（学说）构成，义为「博物馆学」
由 museology 加表示「人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「博物馆学专家」
与 museum 同源于缪斯，义为「沉思；冥想」

senses.title: A building that collects and displays objects
senses.definition: a building where objects of art, history or science are collected, kept and shown to the public
senses.definitionCN: 收藏、保存并向公众展示艺术、历史或科学物品的建筑
senses.example: The museum opens at nine and closes at five.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆九点开门，五点闭馆。
senses.why: Greek mouseion was a place of the Muses, a seat of learning, and the modern word still names a building that holds knowledge rather than sells goods.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mouseion 是缪斯女神的地方，也就是治学之所；现代这个词仍指收藏知识的建筑，而不是卖东西的场所。

senses.title: The institution or collection itself
senses.definition: the institution, or the collection it holds, considered apart from its building
senses.definitionCN: 把这个机构或它收藏的藏品单独来看，而不指建筑本身
senses.example: The museum lent three paintings to a show in another city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆把三幅画借给了另一座城市的展览。
senses.why: Because the collection travels while the building stays, the name moved from the place to the body that owns and cares for the objects.
senses.whyCN: 藏品可以出借巡展，而建筑留在原地，于是这个名称从「地方」转到「拥有并照管这些藏品」的机构。

senses.title: A room devoted to a special subject
senses.definition: a room or gallery set apart for a particular subject, often smaller than a full museum
senses.definitionCN: 为一个特定主题单独辟出的房间或展廊，通常比完整的博物馆小
senses.example: A small museum of typewriters sits above the bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 书店楼上有一间小小的打字机陈列室。
senses.why: When the gathering of objects was small and focused, English kept the same word for a single room, so a museum can be a cabinet-sized space for one subject.
senses.whyCN: 当收藏的对象又少又专时，英语仍用同一个词指单个展室，所以 museum 也可以是为一个主题办的小小空间。

intro.en: Museum goes back to the Greek mouseion, a place of the Muses, and it reached English through Latin and French as a name for a place of study.
intro.cn: museum 可追溯到希腊语 mouseion，即缪斯之地；它经拉丁语与法语进入英语，最初指治学之所。

items.en: Mousa, a Muse, named one of the goddesses of poetry, music and learning, and their shrines were places of the arts.
items.cn: mousa 即缪斯，是掌管诗歌、音乐与学问的女神，供奉她们的地方就是艺术之地。

items.en: Mouseion meant a place dedicated to the Muses, a seat of learning where books and objects were kept and discussed.
items.cn: mouseion 意为献给缪斯的地方，是保存并讨论书籍与器物的治学之所。

items.en: Latin borrowed mouseion as museum, keeping the sense of a study or a place of learned pursuits.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 mouseion 借作 museum，仍指书房或治学之所。

items.en: French musée carried the word into the language of galleries, where it named a place holding a collection open to visitors.
items.cn: 法语 musée 把这个词带进画廊的语言，指收藏并向参观者开放的地方。

items.en: Modern English fixes the idea of a public building, and the Greek word for Muse survives inside muse and music.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义固定为公共建筑，希腊语中「缪斯」这个词仍留在 muse 与 music 里面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Greek Muse and on the place ending -eum; the near-meaning group collects places and events that hold collections.
note.cn: 形近组收由希腊语「缪斯」与表地点的 -eum 词尾构成的词；近义组收收藏与展示藏品的场所和活动。

entries.definition: To think deeply about something, or a source of inspiration; the word shares the Greek Muse.
entries.definitionCN: 沉思，或灵感的来源；与希腊语缪斯同源。

entries.definition: Sounds arranged to be sung or played; the name comes through the Muses.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌唱或演奏而组织的声音；名称经由缪斯而来。

entries.definition: A picture made of small coloured pieces; the shape is close but the origin differs.
entries.definitionCN: 用小块彩色材料拼成的图画；字形相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: A large, grand tomb; the ending looks alike but the word comes from a king's name.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟的陵墓；词尾形似，但这个词来自一位国王的名字。

entries.definition: A room or building where art is shown.
entries.definitionCN: 陈列艺术品的房间或建筑。

entries.definition: A public display of objects or works.
entries.definitionCN: 公开展示物品或作品的活动。

entries.definition: A place or collection of records kept for study.
entries.definitionCN: 为研究保存档案的地方或收藏。

entries.definition: A group of objects gathered and kept together.
entries.definitionCN: 收集并放在一起的一组物品。

normalIntro.en: A Greek place of the Muses became a Latin study, a French gallery and an English public building; the entry follows that journey.
normalIntro.cn: 一个希腊的缪斯之地，先后变成拉丁语的书房、法语的画廊、英语的公共建筑；这个词条就沿着这条路展开。

normal.en: Mouseion was a place of the Muses, so a museum is first of all a home for knowledge, not a shop.
normal.cn: mouseion 是缪斯之地，所以 museum 首先是知识的住所，而不是店铺。

normal.en: The Muses cover poetry and music too, which is why muse and music sit in the same word family.
normal.cn: 缪斯也掌管诗歌与音乐，所以 muse 与 music 留在同一个词族里。

normal.en: -Eum is a place ending borrowed from Greek, so museum, mausoleum and gymnasium share a shape that marks a location.
normal.cn: -eum 是从希腊语借来的地点词尾，所以 museum、mausoleum、gymnasium 共有一个表示场所的形状。

normal.en: English keeps museum for the building, while a gallery can be a single room and a collection can travel.
normal.cn: 英语用 museum 指建筑，而 gallery 可以只是单个房间，collection 则可以出借巡展。

normal.en: Natural history museum joins the word with a subject, which shows the building can be named after what it holds.
normal.cn: natural history museum 把词与一个主题连起来，说明这类建筑可以用所藏之物来命名。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp over a glass case, one cracked pot lit from above.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照在玻璃柜上，一只裂了缝的陶罐被光从上方照亮。

abstract.en: A place named after goddesses of art suggests that objects are kept so they can be read, not merely stored.
abstract.cn: 一个以艺术女神命名的地方，说明藏品被保存下来是为了供人解读，而不只是堆放。

abstract.en: The word began with study and ended with visitors, so a museum is learning made public.
abstract.cn: 这个词从治学开始，以观众收尾，所以博物馆就是把学问向公众打开。

examples.en: The museum was closed for repairs all summer.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆整个夏天都在维修，暂停开放。

examples.en: We spent a rainy afternoon in the natural history museum.
examples.cn: 下雨的下午，我们待在自然史博物馆里。

examples.en: The museum lent its best painting to a foreign exhibition.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆把最好的一幅画借给了国外的展览。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缪泽姆」——缪斯女神住的地方，如今成了博物馆；记住 museum。

root: 希腊语 mousa（缪斯）→ mouseion（缪斯之地，治学之所）→ 拉丁语 museum → 法语 musée → 英语 museum；同族词有 muse、music、museology，没有另立的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place of the Muses; the senses divide into the public building, the institution and its collection, and a single room for one subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是缪斯之地；义项分出公共建筑、机构与馆藏，以及为单一主题设的展室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit glass case holding one cracked pot, with a guide and children in front of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：射灯照着玻璃柜里一只裂陶罐，柜前站着讲解员和孩子。

branches.en: a lit case holding one cracked pot
branches.cn: 射灯照着的一只裂陶罐

branches.en: a crate of paintings sent to another city
branches.cn: 一箱送往另一座城市参展的画

branches.en: a school class walking in behind a guide
branches.cn: 跟着讲解员走进展厅的一个班级

branches.en: a narrow room lined with old typewriters
branches.cn: 摆满旧打字机的狭长展室

branches.en: a name that covers both the walls and the treasures inside them
branches.cn: 一个既指墙壁、也指其中珍藏的名称

intro.en: A Greek noun for the Muses, a Greek place ending and the Latin and English forms built on them hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个表示缪斯的希腊名词、一个希腊地点词尾，以及由它们构成的拉丁语与英语形式，撑起了这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin passed on the Greek place word as museum, so the Latin forms here are borrowings rather than native relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊的地点词转写为 museum，所以这里的拉丁形式是借词，而不是本土同族词。

items.meaning: art of sound through the Muses

latinEntries.meaning: a place of study, a library

definition_zh: 蘑菇；菌类；迅速增长；迅速涌现
definition_en: a fungus that grows above ground with a soft stem and a cap, many kinds of which are eaten; also to grow, spread or appear very quickly
core_image: 雨后草地上几朵圆伞般的白菇一夜之间撑开，挤满了整片泥地
scene: 清晨的草地还带着露水，几朵白伞样的菌子从落叶堆里顶出来，比前一天大了整整一圈。Mushrooms appeared across the lawn after two days of rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「蘑菇、菌类」（第 1 个义项：有菌盖与菌柄的肉质真菌）；句意为连下两天雨后，草坪上冒出了一片蘑菇。图中可辨识物件：露水、落叶堆、白色菌盖。

derivatives.zh: 由 mushroom 加 -ing 构成，义为「迅速增多；采蘑菇」
由 mushroom 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「采蘑菇的人」

senses.title: A fleshy fungus with a stem and a cap
senses.definition: a fungus that grows above ground with a soft stem and a cap, many kinds of which are eaten
senses.definitionCN: 长在地面、有柔软菌柄与菌盖的真菌，其中许多种类可食用
senses.example: She sliced the mushrooms and added them to the pan.
senses.exampleCN: 她把蘑菇切片放进锅里。
senses.why: The English name probably comes from French mousseron, a word for a kind of mushroom, later reshaped by association with moss where the fungi grow.
senses.whyCN: 英语这个词很可能来自法语 mousseron（一种蘑菇），后来又因为菌子多生于苔藓而被改写成形。

senses.title: Fungi as a group in ordinary use
senses.definition: the group of such fungi, especially the edible kinds sold or gathered as food
senses.definitionCN: 这类真菌的整体，尤指市场上出售或采来食用的种类
senses.example: Wild mushrooms are best kept apart from the rest of the shopping.
senses.exampleCN: 野生蘑菇最好和其余买来的东西分开放。
senses.why: Because cooks and foragers deal with many kinds at once, the same word came to name the category in the kitchen rather than one species.
senses.whyCN: 厨师和采菌人一次面对许多种类，于是同一个词在厨房里成了对整个类别的称呼，而不是某一个物种。

senses.title: To increase very fast
senses.definition: to grow, spread or appear very quickly, like fungi rising overnight
senses.definitionCN: 像菌子一夜冒出那样，迅速地增长、扩散或出现
senses.example: Sales mushroomed after the advertisement ran.
senses.exampleCN: 广告播出之后，销量迅速增长。
senses.why: The picture of a fungus swelling up in a single night supplied a ready metaphor for anything that multiplies suddenly.
senses.whyCN: 菌子在夜里一下子撑开的画面，为任何骤然增多的事物提供了现成的比喻。

intro.en: The name of the mushroom is one of the less certain words in English: it is probably French in origin and was later reshaped by English speakers.
intro.cn: 蘑菇这个词的来源在英语里算不上确定：一般认为出自法语，后来被英语使用者改了形状。

items.en: The earliest forms are hard to trace, and dictionaries mark the origin as uncertain rather than settled.
items.cn: 最早的词形难以追溯，词典把来源标为不确定，而不是已有定论。

items.en: A likely source is French mousseron, a name for a kind of mushroom, which English borrowed and altered.
items.cn: 一般认为来源是法语 mousseron，一种蘑菇的名称，英语借入后改动了拼写。

items.en: English speakers seem to have reshaped the word so that it echoed moss, the damp ground where fungi appear.
items.cn: 英语使用者似乎把这个词改得像 moss（苔藓），也就是菌子常出现的潮湿地表。

items.en: By the sixteenth century mushroom and mushrump were both in use for the edible fungus.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，mushroom 与 mushrump 两种写法都用来指可食用的菌类。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling and, from the nineteenth century, extended the word to anything growing with sudden speed.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了拼写，并从十九世纪起把词义扩展到任何迅速增长的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely share the shape of mushroom; the near-meaning group collects fungi, their parts and their relatives.
note.cn: 形近组收只是与 mushroom 字形相近的词；近义组收真菌、真菌的构造以及相关词。

entries.definition: Soft, wet pulp, or a command to a team of dogs; only the opening shape resembles this word.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软湿糊的东西，或对拉雪橇犬发出的口令；只是开头形似。

entries.definition: Soft and wet, or excessively sentimental; the shape is close but the word comes from mash.
entries.definitionCN: 又软又湿的，或过分伤感的；字形相近，但这个词来自 mash。

entries.definition: A small green plant that carpets damp ground; it may have influenced the shape of this word, yet it is a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 铺在潮湿地表的小型绿色植物；它可能影响过这个词的写法，但本身是另一个词。

entries.definition: Low wet ground; the spelling and sound are close, the meaning is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 低洼潮湿之地；拼写与读音相近，意义无关。

entries.definition: Any member of the group that includes moulds, yeasts and mushrooms.
entries.definitionCN: 包括霉菌、酵母与蘑菇在内的一类生物。

entries.definition: An umbrella-shaped fungus, especially a poisonous one.
entries.definitionCN: 伞状真菌，尤指有毒的那种。

entries.definition: The reproductive cell of fungi and other simple organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 真菌等简单生物的繁殖细胞。

entries.definition: A soft fungal growth on damp or decaying matter.
entries.definitionCN: 潮湿物或腐败物上长出的真菌。

normalIntro.en: The origin is uncertain, the spelling echoes moss, and the sudden swelling of a fungus gave English a verb for rapid growth.
normalIntro.cn: 来源不确定，拼写又与苔藓相近，而菌子骤然撑开的画面，给英语提供了一个表示迅速增长的动词。

normal.en: The likely French source mousseron already named a mushroom, so the word arrived with its meaning attached.
normal.cn: 一般认为的法语来源 mousseron 本来就指一种蘑菇，所以这个词是带着意思进来的。

normal.en: The modern spelling echoes moss, and mushrooms do rise from damp mossy ground, which makes the link easy to remember even if it is not the true source.
normal.cn: 现代拼写与 moss（苔藓）相近，蘑菇又真从潮湿的苔藓地里冒出来，所以这层联系即使不是真来源也很好记。

normal.en: Mushroom is both noun and verb, so one shape covers the food and the sudden swelling of numbers.
normal.cn: mushroom 既是名词又是动词，一个形状同时管食物和数量的骤增。

normal.en: The plural mushrooms is usual in the kitchen, while the verb takes mushroomed and mushrooming.
normal.cn: 厨房里常用复数 mushrooms，而动词则取 mushroomed 与 mushrooming。

normal.en: Mushroom cloud borrows the cap shape for the plume of an explosion, showing how far the picture travels.
normal.cn: mushroom cloud 借菌盖的形状来形容爆炸的烟柱，可见这个画面能走多远。

abstract.en: Picture white caps pushing through wet leaves overnight, each one a small umbrella.
abstract.cn: 想象一夜之间，白色菌盖顶开湿叶，每一朵都是一把小伞。

abstract.en: A fungus appears without being planted, which is why the word can mean anything that springs up unplanned.
abstract.cn: 菌子没人种也会出现，所以这个词可以指任何不请自来的东西。

abstract.en: The same shape that feeds people also lends its name to explosions, so mushroom carries both growth and blast.
abstract.cn: 同一个形状既养育人，也给爆炸命名，所以 mushroom 同时带着生长与爆裂。

examples.en: He added mushrooms and cream to the soup.
examples.cn: 他往汤里加了蘑菇和奶油。

examples.en: The small business mushroomed into a chain within three years.
examples.cn: 这家小生意三年之内迅速扩张成了连锁店。

examples.en: Some mushrooms in the wood are poisonous and should not be picked.
examples.cn: 林子里有些蘑菇有毒，不该采。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马什鲁姆」——雨后草地一夜撑开一片小伞；记住 mushroom 是蘑菇。

root: 一般认为源自法语 mousseron（一种蘑菇），英语借入后改写，可能受 moss（苔藓）影响；确切来源不确定，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a cap rising from damp ground; the senses divide into the edible fungus, the group of fungi, and sudden rapid growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从潮湿地表顶出的菌盖；义项分出可食用的菌子、菌类整体，以及突然的迅速增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white caps pushing through wet leaves overnight, each one a small umbrella.
core.cn: 核心意象：一夜之间，白色菌盖顶开湿叶，每一朵都是一把小伞。

branches.en: white caps pushing through wet leaves
branches.cn: 湿叶间顶出的白色菌盖

branches.en: a basket holding several kinds of fungi
branches.cn: 装着几种菌子的一只篮子

branches.en: a chart line rising almost straight up
branches.cn: 几乎笔直上升的曲线

branches.en: a crowd forming at a door in minutes
branches.cn: 几分钟内就在门口聚起的人群

branches.en: one shape that feeds a family and also names a blast
branches.cn: 既喂饱一家人、又给爆炸命名的同一个形状

intro.en: A probable French source, a reshaped ending and two English compounds and suffixes carry this uncertain but vivid word.
intro.cn: 一个很可能的法语来源、一个被改写的词尾，以及几个英语复合形式与后缀，撑起了这个来源不确定却画面鲜明的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: mushroom is probably of French origin, and the word has no settled Latin relative.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：mushroom 一般认为出自法语，并没有确定的拉丁亲属词。

items.meaningCN: 来源不确定的改写词尾

items.meaning: cloud shaped like a cap after an explosion

definition_zh: 音乐；乐曲；乐声；配乐
definition_en: sound shaped by rhythm and melody into an art, together with the pieces it produces and the sound heard when it is performed
core_image: 一根琴弓划过琴弦，空气里浮出有秩序的声响
scene: 琴房里没开灯，雨点敲着窗，桌上一本摊开的乐谱被风翻动。The music from the old piano drifted down the empty corridor.
sceneCN: 这里是「音乐」（第 1 个义项：作为声音艺术的音乐）；句意为旧钢琴的乐声沿着空荡的走廊飘远。可辨识物件：钢琴、乐谱、雨中的窗。

derivatives.zh: 由 music 加 -al 构成，义为「音乐的；悦耳的」
由 music 加 -ian 构成，义为「音乐家；乐手」
由 musical 加 -ly 构成，义为「在音乐上；悦耳地」
由 musician 加 -ship 构成，义为「音乐修养；演奏水准」

senses.title: Organized sound treated as an art
senses.definition: sound arranged in rhythm and melody, made by voices or instruments and valued as an art
senses.definitionCN: 按节奏与旋律安排、由人声或乐器发出并被当作艺术的声音
senses.example: She studied music at the conservatory for four years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在音乐学院学了四年音乐。
senses.why: Greek mousike named the work of the Muses, so the word starts as a disciplined craft rather than as any noise that happens to be loud.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mousikē 原本指缪斯所掌管的技艺，所以这个词的起点是「有章法的技艺」，而不是碰巧很响的杂音。

senses.title: A piece or a body of written works
senses.definition: a particular composition, or the whole set of pieces written by one composer or within one style
senses.definitionCN: 某一首具体的作品，或某位作曲家、某种风格写下的全部作品
senses.example: The orchestra played music by Ravel and Debussy.
senses.exampleCN: 管弦乐队演奏了拉威尔与德彪西的作品。
senses.why: Because one noun can name both the art and the things made by that art, music also points to individual pieces you can put on a programme.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既能指这门艺术，也能指它做出的东西，因此 music 又可以指可以排进节目单的一首首具体作品。

senses.title: The sound actually heard in performance
senses.definition: the audible sound that reaches the ear when instruments or voices are playing
senses.definitionCN: 乐器或人声演奏时真正传到耳朵里的声音
senses.example: From the next room came the music of a violin.
senses.exampleCN: 隔壁房间传来小提琴的乐声。
senses.why: The abstract art becomes audible only at the moment of playing, so the same noun also names the physical sound filling the room.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的艺术只有在演奏的那一刻才变得可听，于是同一个名词也用来指充满房间的实际声响。

senses.title: Music laid under a film, game or ceremony
senses.definition: music used behind another activity to support its mood or mark its moments
senses.definitionCN: 垫在另一项活动之下、用来烘托气氛或标记节点的音乐
senses.example: The film's music does most of the emotional work.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的情绪多半由配乐承担。
senses.why: Once music is thought of as a layer under something else, the word takes the role of accompaniment, from cinema to a graduation ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 当音乐被看成垫在别的东西下面的一层，这个词就承担了伴奏的角色，从电影到毕业典礼都是如此。

intro.en: Music reaches English from the Greek art of the Muses by way of Latin and French, and its meaning widened from one craft to works, sound and accompaniment.
intro.cn: music 从希腊语中「缪斯的技艺」出发，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，词义也从一门技艺扩展到作品、声响与伴奏。

items.en: Mousike was the art presided over by the Muses and covered poetry, song and dance rather than instrumental playing alone.
items.cn: mousikē 是缪斯掌管的技艺，包括诗歌、歌唱与舞蹈，并不只指器乐演奏。

items.en: Latin took the word as musica and used it for the art of sound, one of the disciplines of the medieval schools.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词写作 musica，用来指声音的艺术，是中世纪学校里的学科之一。

items.en: Old French musique carried the word into everyday use for music and for the notation that records it.
items.cn: 古法语 musique 把这个词带入日常使用，既指音乐，也指记录音乐的谱子。

items.en: Middle English music named both the art and a written score, and the two meanings stayed side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语的 music 同时指这门艺术和一份写下的乐谱，两个含义并行了数百年。

items.en: Modern English adds the performed sound and the music written for films and ceremonies, so one word covers art, work, sound and setting.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上演奏出来的声响以及为电影、典礼写的配乐，一个词于是覆盖艺术、作品、声音与场景四层。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the forms built on this stem; the near-meaning group collects the things a piece of music is made of.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词干构成的同族形式；近义组收构成一段音乐的基本元素。

entries.definition: The adjective built on music with -al, meaning of music or sounding pleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 由 music 加 -al 构成的形容词，义为「音乐的」或「悦耳的」。

entries.definition: The person noun built on music with -ian, meaning one who plays or writes music.
entries.definitionCN: 由 music 加 -ian 构成的名词，指演奏或创作音乐的人。

entries.definition: The skill of a musician, formed by adding -ship to musician.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musician 后加 -ship 构成，指音乐家的演奏修养。

entries.definition: The adverb from musical, meaning in a way connected with music.
entries.definitionCN: 由 musical 派生出的副词，义为「在音乐方面」。

entries.definition: The sequence of notes that carries a tune.
entries.definitionCN: 承载曲调的连续音。

entries.definition: A short melody you can hum or whistle.
entries.definitionCN: 可以哼唱或吹出的短曲调。

entries.definition: A piece meant to be sung, words and music together.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌唱而作的作品，词与曲合一。

normalIntro.en: The word is the base of a small family, and the family shows how one noun grows an adjective, a person and a quality.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一小族词的基干，这一族词演示了一个名词如何长出形容词、人物名词和抽象品质。

normal.en: Music is the base of the family: add -al for the adjective musical, add -ian for the person musician.
normal.cn: music 是这一族词的基干：加 -al 得到形容词 musical，加 -ian 得到表示人的 musician。

normal.en: The Greek source mousike meant the art of the Muses, and museum comes from the same shrine, so the two words began as neighbours.
normal.cn: 希腊语 mousikē 意为缪斯的技艺，museum 也出自缪斯的神庙，两个词在源头上是邻居。

normal.en: Music is uncountable, so you say a piece of music or a lot of music, never a music.
normal.cn: music 不可数，所以要说 a piece of music 或 a lot of music，不能说 a music。

normal.en: Sheet music is the written notes rather than the sound, which is why the phrase turns up in every score shop.
normal.cn: sheet music 指纸上写下的音符而不是声响，所以这个说法总出现在卖乐谱的地方。

normal.en: Music to my ears is a fixed idiom for news that makes you glad to hear it.
normal.cn: music to my ears 是固定习语，指让人听了高兴的消息。

abstract.en: Picture the hush in a hall just before the conductor raises a hand: music is what fills that silence on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象音乐厅里指挥抬手前的那片安静：音乐就是有意填满这片安静的东西。

abstract.en: One noun covering art, works and background sound shows how deeply music is layered into ordinary days.
abstract.cn: 一个名词同时覆盖艺术、作品与背景声音，说明音乐早已层层嵌进平常的日子。

abstract.en: If you can hum it, it is already music, even before anyone writes it down.
abstract.cn: 只要你能把它哼出来，它就已经是音乐，哪怕还没有人把它记下来。

examples.en: She writes music for films and games.
examples.cn: 她为电影和游戏作曲。

examples.en: The music was so loud that we could feel the bass through the floor.
examples.cn: 音乐声太大，隔着地板都能感到低音的震动。

examples.en: He stood listening to the music of a street violinist.
examples.cn: 他站着听一位街头小提琴手的琴声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪齐克」：缪斯女神一抬手，音乐就响了；记住 music 是音乐。

root: 一般认为来自希腊语 mousikē（缪斯的技艺），经拉丁语 musica、古法语 musique 进入英语；同族词围绕「音乐」与「做音乐的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is organized sound valued as an art; from it the word reaches the works themselves, the sound heard while playing, and music placed under another activity.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被当作艺术的有序声音；由此分出具体的作品、演奏时听到的声响，以及垫在别的活动之下的配乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bow crossing a string and turning silence into ordered sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：琴弓划过琴弦，把寂静变成有秩序的声响。

branches.en: a practice room where scales slowly become a piece
branches.cn: 琴房里音阶慢慢连成一首曲子

branches.en: a shelf of scores filed under one composer's name
branches.cn: 按一位作曲家名字归档的一架乐谱

branches.en: an orchestra reading a new score for the first time
branches.cn: 乐团第一次读一份新总谱

branches.en: a violin's sound reaching the room next door
branches.cn: 小提琴的声音传到隔壁房间

branches.en: a soundtrack swelling under a closing scene
branches.cn: 片尾画面下渐渐涨起的配乐

intro.en: The family is built on the noun music plus two suffixes: -al for the adjective and -ian for the person, with Latin musica underneath all of them.
intro.cn: 这一族词建立在名词 music 之上，再加 -al 构成形容词、加 -ian 构成指人的名词，底下则是拉丁语 musica。

latinIntro.en: Latin musica came from Greek mousike and became the medieval European word for the art of sound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 musica 来自希腊语 mousikē，后来成为中世纪欧洲指「声音的艺术」的词。

items.meaning: a person who plays or writes music

latinEntries.meaning: of music, and also a musician

definition_zh: 音乐的；悦耳的；有音乐天赋的；音乐剧
definition_en: connected with music, pleasant to hear like music, gifted at music, and also a stage show built from songs and dialogue
core_image: 舞台幕布升起，歌声与对白在同一束灯光里交替
scene: 排练厅的灯亮到深夜，演员们把同一段合唱重复了一遍又一遍。The cast rehearsed the new musical until the lights went out.
sceneCN: 这里是「音乐剧」（第 3 个义项：歌曲与对白交替推进的舞台作品）；句意为演员们排练这部新音乐剧，直到灯都灭了。

pos.zh: 音乐的；悦耳的；有音乐天赋的

collocations.zh: 音乐剧剧场；音乐剧艺术

derivatives.zh: 由 musical 加 -ly 构成，义为「在音乐上；悦耳地」
由 musical 加 -ity 构成，义为「音乐性；音乐感」
由 music 加 -ian 构成，指「音乐家」，与 musical 同出 music，并非由 musical 派生

senses.title: Connected with music as an art
senses.definition: belonging to music, or used in the making and study of music
senses.definitionCN: 属于音乐的，或用于创作与研究音乐的
senses.example: She has a musical ear and can pick out a tune after one hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一双音乐的耳朵，听一遍就能把曲调挑出来。
senses.why: The Latin suffix -alis turned musica into musicalis, meaning 'belonging to music', so this sense is the plain label the suffix was made for.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -alis 把 musica 变成 musicalis，意思就是「属于音乐的」，所以这个义项正是该后缀的本职。

senses.title: Pleasant to hear, as if sung
senses.definition: sounding sweet and rhythmical, the way a well-made melody sounds
senses.definitionCN: 听起来甜美而有节奏，像一段做得好的旋律
senses.example: Their voices blended into a musical murmur.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的嗓音融成一片悦耳的低语。
senses.why: A sound orderly enough to resemble music earns the same adjective, so the word moves from 'belonging to music' to 'sounding like music' and becomes praise.
senses.whyCN: 一种声音只要有序到近似音乐，就能用同一个形容词，于是词义从「属于音乐」滑到「像音乐一样好听」，变成一句称赞。

senses.title: A stage or screen work of songs and dialogue
senses.definition: a play or film in which songs and spoken scenes alternate, usually with dancing
senses.definitionCN: 歌曲与说白交替出现、通常还带舞蹈的舞台剧或影片
senses.example: The cast rehearsed the new musical until the lights went out.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们排练这部新音乐剧，直到灯都灭了。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century playbills shortened musical comedy to musical, and the adjective became a noun for an entire kind of show.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的戏单把 musical comedy 缩成 musical，这个形容词于是名词化，指一整类舞台作品。

senses.title: Gifted at music or sensitive to it
senses.definition: naturally aware of pitch and rhythm, or able to play and sing well
senses.definitionCN: 天生对音高与节奏敏感，或演奏演唱得好
senses.example: Even as a child he was unusually musical.
senses.exampleCN: 他小时候就显露出不寻常的音乐天赋。
senses.why: A person whose ear is tuned to music is described by the same adjective, so the word shifts from the art itself to the gift in the person.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵对音乐敏感的人也用这个形容词来描述，于是词义从艺术本身转到人身上的天赋。

intro.en: Musical is the adjective built on Latin musica with the suffix -alis; its noun use for a stage show came much later, from the theatre.
intro.cn: musical 是用后缀 -alis 加在拉丁语 musica 上构成的形容词；指舞台作品的名词用法要晚得多，来自剧院。

items.en: The Greek adjective mousikos described anything of the Muses, including a person trained in song and dance.
items.cn: 希腊语形容词 mousikos 形容一切属于缪斯的东西，也包括受过歌唱与舞蹈训练的人。

items.en: Latin kept musica for the art itself, the noun from which a whole set of adjectives could be built.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 musica 指这门艺术本身，这个名词后来又长出一整组形容词。

items.en: Musicalis added -alis to musica and meant simply 'relating to music', with no hint yet of the stage.
items.cn: musicalis 在 musica 后加 -alis，意思只是「与音乐有关的」，当时还没有舞台的含义。

items.en: Middle French passed musical to English, where it first described anything of music, from voices to instruments.
items.cn: 中古法语把 musical 传给英语，英语最初用它形容一切与音乐有关的东西，从嗓音到乐器。

items.en: In the nineteenth century musical was clipped from musical comedy and became a noun for a show of songs and spoken scenes.
items.cn: 十九世纪，musical 由 musical comedy 缩略而来，变成指「歌曲与说白并存的舞台作品」的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjective's own family and adverbs; the near-meaning group collects words for sounds that please the ear.
note.cn: 形近组收这个形容词的同族形式与副词；近义组收形容声音悦耳的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective is built on, naming the art of sound.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词所依附的名词，指声音的艺术。

entries.definition: The person noun from the same base, formed with -ian rather than -al.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的指人名词，用 -ian 而非 -al 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb built on musical with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musical 后加 -ly 构成的副词。

entries.definition: The noun built on musical with -ity, naming the quality of being musical.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musical 后加 -ity 构成的名词，指音乐性。

entries.definition: Relating to melody, or pleasant because of its melody.
entries.definitionCN: 与旋律有关的；因旋律而动听的。

entries.definition: Having a pleasant tune that is easy to hear and follow.
entries.definitionCN: 曲调优美、容易听清的。

entries.definition: Sweet-sounding, like a well-sung melody.
entries.definitionCN: 音调甜美的，像唱得好的旋律。

normalIntro.en: The adjective sits between the noun music and the person musician, and its suffixes show which one you mean.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词夹在名词 music 与指人的 musician 之间，后缀决定你指的是哪一边。

normal.en: The suffix -al turns the noun music into the adjective musical, just as nation becomes national.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 把名词 music 变成形容词 musical，就像 nation 变成 national 一样。

normal.en: The -al ending marks a quality, while -ian marks a person, which is the clean line between musical and musician.
normal.cn: -al 结尾标记性质，-ian 结尾标记人物，这就是 musical 与 musician 之间清楚的分界。

normal.en: The noun musical began as a short form of musical comedy on nineteenth-century playbills.
normal.cn: 名词 musical 起初是十九世纪戏单上 musical comedy 的缩略形式。

normal.en: A musical instrument is any instrument used for music, a fixed phrase that pins the adjective to its first sense.
normal.cn: a musical instrument 指任何用于音乐的乐器，这个固定搭配把形容词钉在第一个义项上。

normal.en: Musicality is musical plus -ity: the quality of having a musical ear, named as a noun.
normal.cn: musicality 是 musical 加 -ity，把「有音乐耳朵」这种性质变成名词。

abstract.en: One adjective describing a sound, a show and a person's ear shows how a single idea spreads over three very different things.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词既能形容声音、又能形容演出、还能形容人的耳朵，说明一个想法可以铺开到三种很不同的事物上。

abstract.en: When applause follows a song, the adjective quietly turns into a noun without changing a single letter.
abstract.cn: 歌声之后掌声响起，这个形容词便悄悄变成名词，一个字母都没改。

abstract.en: Calling a voice musical is a compliment that measures a human sound against an art form.
abstract.cn: 说一副嗓音 musical，是拿人的声音去比照一门艺术，本身就是称赞。

examples.en: The musical instruments were stored in a padded case.
examples.cn: 乐器被存放在一个带衬垫的箱子里。

examples.en: Her speaking voice is low and musical.
examples.cn: 她说话的声音低沉而悦耳。

examples.en: Tickets for the new musical sold out within a week.
examples.cn: 这部新音乐剧的门票一周内售罄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪齐扣」：缪斯一开口，歌声就扣住人；记住 musical 是音乐的、音乐剧。

root: 一般认为来自晚期拉丁语 musicalis（由 musica 加 -alis 构成），经中古法语 musical 进入英语；名词「音乐剧」是 musical comedy 的缩略。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts as a plain label for anything of music; it then stretches to sounds that please the ear, to a person's ear for music, and finally becomes a noun for a stage show.
sensesIntro.cn: 形容词最初只是「与音乐有关」的标签；随后扩展到悦耳的声音、人的音乐耳朵，最后名词化为一种舞台作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stage curtain rising on a song that carries the story forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台幕布升起，一首歌把故事往前推。

branches.en: a rehearsal room with a piano and a metronome
branches.cn: 摆着钢琴与节拍器的排练房

branches.en: a voice so smooth that the room goes quiet
branches.cn: 嗓音顺滑到让整个房间安静下来

branches.en: a child picking out a tune by ear
branches.cn: 孩子凭耳朵挑出一段曲调

branches.en: a curtain rising on dancers and singers
branches.cn: 幕布升起，舞者与歌者同台

branches.en: an audition settled by the quality of a voice
branches.cn: 由嗓音好坏决定结果的试演

intro.en: The adjective is music plus -al, and two further suffixes, -ly and -ity, turn it into an adverb and a quality noun.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是 music 加 -al，再加 -ly 与 -ity 两个后缀，就得到副词和表示性质的名词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin musicalis is the direct model: musica plus -alis, meaning simply belonging to music.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 musicalis 是直接的样板：musica 加 -alis，意思就是「属于音乐的」。

latinEntries.meaning: of music, and also a musician

definition_zh: 突变；变异；（一般意义上的）变化；语音换音
definition_en: a change in genetic material, the process that produces such a change, or a change of form in a broader sense
core_image: 复制过程中一个字母被换掉，整段指令的意思随之改变，纸带上留下一个明显的错位
scene: 复制过程中一个字母被换掉，整段指令的意思随之改变。A single mutation can switch off a gene that controls cell division.
sceneCN: 这里 mutation 指「遗传物质中的一个改变」（第 1 个义项：基因序列的变化）；句意为一个突变就能关闭控制细胞分裂的基因。可辨识物件：复制纸带、错位字母、红色标记、基因示意图。

senses.title: A change in genetic material
senses.definition: an alteration in the sequence or structure of genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质序列或结构的改变
senses.example: A mutation in the control region increased the plant's height.
senses.exampleCN: 控制区的一个突变增加了这株植物的高度。
senses.why: The technical sense is a change at the level of instructions, which is why it can be small in size and large in effect.
senses.whyCN: 技术义指指令层面的改变，因此它可以很小，却产生很大影响。

senses.title: The process that produces variation
senses.definition: the process by which genetic changes arise and supply variation
senses.definitionCN: 遗传改变产生并提供变异的过程
senses.example: Mutation supplies the variation on which selection acts.
senses.exampleCN: 突变为自然选择提供作用其上的变异。
senses.why: As a process, mutation is a source rather than an event, so it appears without an article in population genetics.
senses.whyCN: 作为过程，突变是来源而非事件，因此在群体遗传学中常不带冠词。

senses.title: An organism carrying a change
senses.definition: an organism or strain that carries an altered genetic sequence
senses.definitionCN: 携带改变后遗传序列的生物体或品系
senses.example: The lab keeps a pale-eyed mutation in its fly stocks.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在果蝇品系中保存着一个浅色眼的突变体。
senses.why: Laboratory usage shortens 'a mutant organism' to 'a mutation', especially when the change is the point of interest.
senses.whyCN: 实验室用法把「突变体生物」缩短为「一个突变」，尤其当改变本身是研究重点时。

senses.title: A general change of form
senses.titleCN: 一般意义上的变化、转变
senses.definition: a change in form, character or policy
senses.definitionCN: 形态、性质或政策上的变化
senses.example: The policy underwent several mutations before adoption.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策在通过前经历了几次变化。
senses.why: The older general sense survives outside biology, where mutation means transformation rather than sequence change.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的一般义在生物学之外存续，那里的 mutation 指转变，而非序列改变。

senses.title: Vowel mutation in linguistics
senses.definition: a change in a vowel caused by a following sound, as in umlaut
senses.definitionCN: 由后接音引起的元音变化，如日耳曼语变音
senses.example: The plural shows mutation of the root vowel.
senses.exampleCN: 复数形式显示出词根元音的换音。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century philology used mutation for sound change, a sense older than the genetic one.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪语文学用 mutation 指语音变化，这一义比遗传义更早。

senses.title: Mutation rate
senses.definition: the frequency with which genetic changes arise per generation or unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 每代或每单位时间出现遗传改变的频率
senses.example: Mutation rate depends on repair efficiency.
senses.exampleCN: 突变率取决于修复效率。
senses.why: Measuring changes turns them into a rate, which is why mutation appears in quantitative genetics as a number.
senses.whyCN: 测量改变使其成为比率，因此在数量遗传学中 mutation 以一个数字出现。

senses.title: Mutation breeding
senses.definition: the use of induced genetic changes to produce new varieties
senses.definitionCN: 利用诱发的遗传改变产生新品种
senses.example: Mutation breeding produced a shorter rice variety.
senses.exampleCN: 突变育种产生了一种更矮的水稻品种。
senses.why: Breeding treats mutation as a tool: changes are induced, then selected, without inserting foreign sequences.
senses.whyCN: 育种把突变当作工具：诱发改变后再选择，不插入外来序列。

senses.title: Neutral, harmful or beneficial
senses.titleCN: 中性、有害或有利的突变
senses.definition: a genetic change classified by its effect on the organism
senses.definitionCN: 按对生物体的影响分类的遗传改变
senses.example: Most mutations are neutral, a few are harmful, and a very few help.
senses.exampleCN: 多数突变是中性的，少数有害，极少数有利。
senses.why: The word does not build harm into its meaning; effects are added by the adjectives that surround it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身不含「有害」，影响是由周围的形容词加上的。

intro.en: Mutation comes from Latin mutatio 'a change', from mutare 'to change'. English used it for general change before genetics gave it a technical sense.
intro.cn: mutation 来自拉丁 mutatio「变化」，源自动词 mutare「改变」。在遗传学赋予它技术义之前，英语已用它表示一般变化。

items.en: Mutare 'to change' is the base of mutatio. Its deeper origin is not established beyond Latin, so any pre-Latin root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mutare「改变」是 mutatio 的基础。它在拉丁语之外的更深来源未得到确证，因此任何拉丁语之前的词根均属重构。

items.en: Mutatio 'a change' was formed with -tio, the action-noun suffix, from the past participle stem mutat-.
items.cn: mutatio「变化」由过去分词词干 mutat- 加动作名词后缀 -tio 构成。

items.en: Mutation entered English in the fourteenth century with the general sense 'change, alteration'; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: mutation 在 14 世纪以「变化、改动」的一般义进入英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century genetics gave mutation the technical sense of a change in hereditary material; the genetic sense is recorded from 1894.
items.cn: 19 世纪末至 20 世纪初的遗传学赋予 mutation「遗传物质改变」的技术义；遗传义从 1894 年起有记录。

items.en: Nineteenth-century philology used mutation for vowel change, especially umlaut; the term i-mutation is recorded from 1874.
items.cn: 19 世纪语文学用 mutation 指元音变化，尤其是变音；i-mutation 这一术语从 1874 年起有记录。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin and sense dates): mutare has no established deeper etymology, and the boundary between general and biological use is not sharply dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前词源与义项年代）：mutare 没有已确立的更深词源，一般义与生物学义的分界也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one separates mutation from its family and from a dangerous look-alike; group two separates it from words for variation and change.
note.cn: 第一组把 mutation 与其词族及一个易混形近词分开；第二组把它与「变异」「变化」类词区分。

entries.definition: The verb meaning 'to undergo or cause a mutation'; mutation is the event or process.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「发生或导致突变」的动词；mutation 是事件或过程。

entries.definition: An organism carrying a mutation, or the adjective describing it; it is a noun of the changed body.
entries.definitionCN: 携带突变的生物体，或描述它的形容词；指被改变的身体。

entries.definition: Relating to a mutation; the adjective does not name the change itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与突变相关的；形容词不命名改变本身。

entries.definition: From mutilare 'to maim, cut off', not mutare: the act of damaging or removing a part. The resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 mutilare「残害、割去」，并非 mutare：指损伤或割除某一部分。相似是偶然的。

entries.definition: Difference among individuals; mutation is one source of variation, not variation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 群体内个体间的差异；突变是变异的来源之一，并非变异本身。

entries.definition: A change in something, often deliberate; mutation stresses a change in form or sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的改变，常为有意；mutation 强调形态或序列的改变。

entries.definition: The broad everyday word; mutation is narrower and often technical.
entries.definitionCN: 宽泛的日常用词；mutation 更窄，常带技术性。

entries.definition: A complete change of form, often dramatic; mutation can be a single small change.
entries.definitionCN: 形态的彻底改变，常较剧烈；mutation 可以是单个微小改变。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mutare 'to change' + -tion: the act of changing.
normal.cn: mutare「改变」+ -tion：改变的行为。

normal.en: The family runs mutate, mutation, mutant and mutational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mutate、mutation、mutant 与 mutational。

normal.en: Mutation rate, point mutation and mutation breeding are fixed phrases.
normal.cn: 突变率、点突变与突变育种是固定搭配。

normal.en: Mutation is not automatically harmful: most changes are neutral.
normal.cn: 突变并非自动有害：多数改变是中性的。

normal.en: Linguistic mutation means vowel change, an older sense.
normal.cn: 语言学中的 mutation 指元音换音，是更早的义项。

abstract.en: Picture a single wrong letter turning a recipe into a different dish.
abstract.cn: 想象一个错字母把食谱变成另一道菜。

abstract.en: Picture a copying machine that occasionally drops a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一台复印机偶尔漏掉一个记号。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour changing as it passes from mouth to mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻在口耳相传中改变。

examples.en: The mutation was traced to a single base change.
examples.cn: 这个突变被追溯到单个碱基改变。

examples.en: Mutation is the raw material of evolution.
examples.cn: 突变是进化的原料。

examples.en: The old word underwent a mutation in meaning over two centuries.
examples.cn: 这个旧词在两个世纪里经历了词义变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: mut（改变）+ ation（名词尾）——改变的结果 → 突变；一般义是「变化」。

root: 拉丁 mutatio「变化」← mutare「改变」；mutare 在拉丁语之外的更深来源不确定，相关原始印欧语词根均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one changed unit: the change itself, the process, the carrier, a general alteration, a vowel shift, a rate, a breeding tool and a classification by effect.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个被改变的单位展开：改变本身、过程、携带者、一般变化、元音换音、比率、育种工具与按效果分类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one letter replaced during copying, and the meaning of the whole strip shifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：复制时一个字母被替换，整条纸带的意思随之改变。

branches.en: CHANGE AND SOURCE: a change in the material, and the process that keeps supplying it.
branches.cn: 改变与来源：物质中的改变，以及不断提供改变的过程。

branches.en: CARRIER AND EFFECT: an organism that carries the change, and how its effect is classified.
branches.cn: 携带者与效果：携带改变的生物体，以及效果如何分类。

branches.en: GENERAL CHANGE: policy and form can mutate outside biology.
branches.cn: 一般变化：政策与形态在生物学之外也能改变。

branches.en: VOWEL CHANGE: philology used the word for sound shift before genetics did.
branches.cn: 元音变化：语文学在遗传学之前就用这个词指语音转变。

branches.en: MEASURE AND TOOL: a rate to count, and a breeding method to use.
branches.cn: 度量与工具：可计数的比率，以及可使用的育种方法。

intro.en: Mutation is a Latin action noun; its stem also builds the verb, the carrier noun and the adjective, and the same root appears in words for change and unchangeability.
intro.cn: mutation 是拉丁动作名词；其词干还构成动词、携带者名词与形容词，同一词根也出现在表示「可变」与「不可变」的词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutare gives mutate, mutation, mutant and mutable; com- and in- build commutation and immutable, trans- builds transmutation. All belong to the same changing root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mutare 衍生 mutate、mutation、mutant 与 mutable；com- 与 in- 构成 commutation 与 immutable，trans- 构成 transmutation。它们都属同一「改变」词根。

items.example: The root names the act of changing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名改变的动作。

items.example: Mutatio is the direct source of mutation.
items.exampleCN: mutatio 是 mutation 的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix makes an action noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成动作名词。

items.example: Commutation of a sentence reduced the penalty.
The transmutation of elements was once alchemy.
items.exampleCN: 元素转变曾属于炼金术。

definition_zh: 相互的；彼此的；共同的（后一义常被批评为宽松用法）
definition_en: given, felt, or done by each side toward the other in exchange; also shared in common by two or more parties
core_image: 两只手同时递出同一把钥匙：你给我，我也给你
scene: 两位邻居隔着栅栏交换对方大门的钥匙，各替对方保管一把备用钥匙。Two neighbours stand at the fence and hand each other a key to the other's gate; their help is mutual, since each one keeps a spare key for the other.
sceneCN: 这里 mutual 是「互相给予、彼此交换」（第 1 个义项：两方对等地给出并接受）；句意：两位邻居站在篱笆边，各自把对方院门的钥匙递给对方，他们的帮助是相互的，因为各自都为对方留了一把备用钥匙。图中可辨识物件：木篱笆、两把钥匙、两只同时伸出的手、两扇院门；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Reciprocally given: both sides exchange
senses.titleCN: 互相给予：两边都在交换
senses.definition: given by each side to the other, so that what one gives is returned in kind
senses.definitionCN: 一方给出的，另一方也以同类回报；给予与接受同时发生在两边
senses.example: Their help was mutual: each repaired what the other had broken.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的帮助是相互的：各自修好了对方弄坏的东西。
senses.why: Late 15c. mutual was first used of feelings and meant 'reciprocally given and received'. The core picture is an exchange: I give, you give back.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪晚期 mutual 最先用于感情，义为“相互给予并接受”。核心画面是一次交换：我给，你也给回来。

senses.title: Mutual affection: a feeling each holds for the other
senses.titleCN: 相互的情感：各自对对方怀有同样的心
senses.definition: of a feeling, held by two people each toward the other, so that the regard is returned
senses.definitionCN: 指一种情感，两人各自对对方怀有，因而这份心意是被回应的
senses.example: The mutual affection between the two sisters lasted all their lives.
senses.exampleCN: 两姐妹之间的相互关爱持续了一生。
senses.why: A feeling can itself be the thing exchanged. Each heart holds the same regard, so the emotion is returned rather than held on one side only.
senses.whyCN: 情感本身就可以是被交换的东西。两颗心怀着同样的心意，因此这份情感是被回应的，而不是只停留在一边。

senses.title: The disputed mutual friend: a person known to both
senses.titleCN: 备受争议的 mutual friend：两人都认识的人
senses.definition: a person whom two other people both know, whether or not those two know each other through that person
senses.definitionCN: 两个人都认识的人，不论这两人是否正因此人而相识
senses.example: We met through a mutual friend at the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 我们经一位共同的朋友在博物馆相识。
senses.why: The 1630s 'common' sense let mutual describe what two parties share. Victorian critics attacked a mutual friend because a friend is not exchanged, yet the phrase is now standard.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 30 年代出现的“共同”义，让 mutual 可以形容两方共享之物。维多利亚时代的批评者攻击 a mutual friend，因为朋友并不是被“交换”的；但这一说法如今已属标准。

senses.title: Shared in common: a quality both possess
senses.titleCN: 共同拥有：两方都具有的性质
senses.definition: held or possessed in common by two or more parties, with no idea of exchange
senses.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同持有或拥有，不含交换之意
senses.example: Their mutual interest in birds began at the same observatory.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对鸟类的共同兴趣始于同一座观测站。
senses.why: From the 1630s mutual widened from exchange to possession: two parties hold the same thing. This branch is the loose 'common' use that style guides still argue about.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 30 年代起，mutual 从“交换”扩展到“持有”：两方握着同一样东西。这条分支就是用法指南至今仍在争论的宽松“共同”义。

senses.title: Mutual benefit: advantage that runs both ways
senses.definition: producing advantage for each of the parties involved, so that neither gains at the other's expense
senses.definitionCN: 为涉及的每一方都带来好处，没有一方以另一方受损为代价获利
senses.example: The trade deal was based on mutual benefit rather than charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这项贸易协定建立在互利而非施舍之上。
senses.why: Benefit follows the exchange image: each side hands over something and receives something in return, so the gain travels in both directions.
senses.whyCN: benefit 延续了交换意象：每一方交出一些东西，又得到一些回报，因此好处是双向流动的。

senses.title: Mutual agreement: a promise binding both sides
senses.titleCN: 双方协议：约束两边的承诺
senses.definition: an arrangement accepted by both parties and binding each of them equally
senses.definitionCN: 两方都接受、并同等约束双方的安排
senses.example: They ended the lease by mutual agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们经双方同意终止了租约。
senses.why: An agreement is exchanged as promises: each gives a pledge and receives one. Because both are bound, the obligation is mutual in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: 协议是以承诺作交换：各方给出一份保证，也收到一份保证。由于双方都受约束，这种义务是严格意义上的“相互的”。

senses.title: Mutual insurance: a company owned by its members
senses.titleCN: 互助保险：由会员共同拥有的公司
senses.definition: of an insurer or society owned by its policyholders, who share the risks and the profits
senses.definitionCN: 指由保单持有人共同拥有的保险机构，成员分担风险、共享收益
senses.example: The mutual insurance society returned part of the premium to every member.
senses.exampleCN: 这家互助保险社把部分保费返还给每位成员。
senses.why: Members pay in and cover one another, so the exchange is pooled rather than one-to-one. Mutual names the arrangement in which each member is both payer and owner.
senses.whyCN: 成员缴钱并相互保障，交换因此被汇聚起来，而不是一对一进行。mutual 命名的是这样一种安排：每个成员既是付款人又是所有者。

senses.title: Mutual fund: money pooled and shared
senses.titleCN: 共同基金：汇集并共享的资金
senses.definition: a fund in which many investors pool money and share the returns, recorded from 1950
senses.definitionCN: 众多投资者汇集资金并共享收益的基金，该说法记录于 1950 年
senses.example: She put her savings into a mutual fund rather than a single stock.
senses.exampleCN: 她把积蓄投入共同基金，而不是单只股票。
senses.why: Here mutual marks a pool: every investor holds a share of the same whole. The exchange is between members and the fund, and the ownership is shared.
senses.whyCN: 这里 mutual 标记的是一口“资金池”：每位投资者都持有同一整体的份额。交换发生在成员与基金之间，所有权则是共享的。

senses.title: Mutual relation: each term implies the other
senses.titleCN: 相互关系：每一项都蕴含另一项
senses.definition: in logic and mathematics, of a relation in which each of two terms entails or points to the other
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑与数学中，指两项之间每一项都蕴含或指向另一项的关系
senses.example: In logic, entailment is mutual when each of two propositions follows from the other.
senses.exampleCN: 在逻辑中，当两个命题各自都能推出对方时，蕴含关系就是相互的。
senses.why: The exchange becomes formal: A gives support to B and B gives support back to A. Mutual relation names this perfect two-way dependency.
senses.whyCN: 交换在这里变得形式化：A 给 B 支撑，B 也给 A 支撑。mutual relation 命名的是这种完美的双向依赖。

senses.title: Mutual assured destruction: a guarantee aimed both ways
senses.titleCN: 相互确保摧毁：对准两边的保证
senses.definition: the Cold War doctrine that a full nuclear exchange would destroy both sides, so neither would strike first; abbreviated MAD in 1966
senses.definitionCN: 冷战理论：全面核交换将摧毁双方，因此谁都不敢先动手；1966 年缩写为 MAD
senses.example: Mutual assured destruction gave the Cold War its strangest acronym, MAD.
senses.exampleCN: 相互确保摧毁给冷战留下了最古怪的缩写 MAD。
senses.why: Each side guarantees the other's destruction, so the threat is returned in full. The word's exchange core hardens into a deadly symmetry.
senses.whyCN: 每一方都保证对方的毁灭，威胁被完整地回敬过去。这个词的“交换”核心在这里硬化成一种致命的对称。

intro.en: Mutual entered English in the late 15c. from Old French mutuel, and its first sense was an exchange of feeling, not joint ownership. The 'common' sense is a later and often criticised extension.
intro.cn: mutual 于 15 世纪晚期从古法语 mutuel 进入英语，最初的义项是情感的交换，而不是共同拥有。“共同”义是后来出现、且常受批评的扩展。

items.en: First recorded in the late 15c., used of feelings in the sense 'reciprocally given and received'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 15 世纪晚期，用于感情，义为“相互给予并接受”。

items.en: From Old French mutuel (14c.), which passed the Latin adjective into French.
items.cn: 来自古法语 mutuel（14 世纪），该词把拉丁语形容词带入了法语。

items.en: Latin mutuus meant 'reciprocal, done in exchange'; the stem mut- carries the idea of change and exchange.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus 意为“相互的、交换而成的”；词干 mut- 带有“改变、交换”的意思。

items.en: Traced to PIE *mei-(1) 'to change, go, move'. Watkins adds that its derivatives concern goods and services exchanged by custom or law.
items.cn: 可追溯至原始印欧语 *mei-(1)“改变、去、移动”。Watkins 补充说，该词根的衍生词与社会中按习俗或法律进行的货物与服务交换有关。

items.en: The sense 'common, shared' appears in the 1630s and was already noted as loosely misused, especially in a mutual friend.
items.cn: “共同的、共享的”义在 17 世纪 30 年代出现，当时就已被指出常被宽松误用，尤其见于 a mutual friend。

items.en: Mutual fund is recorded from 1950 and mutual assured destruction, or MAD, from 1966; both keep the two-way picture.
items.cn: mutual fund 记录于 1950 年，mutual assured destruction（缩写 MAD）记录于 1966 年；两者都保留了双向的画面。

note.en: The first group shares the mut- stem or sound, the second shares the meaning of two-way or shared, so form and sense stay apart.
note.cn: 第一组共享 mut- 词干或读音，第二组共享“双向／共享”的词义，这样词形与词义不会被混为一谈。

entries.definition: liable to change. It comes from Latin mutare 'to change', the same PIE family as mutuus, but means changeable rather than exchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 易变的。它来自拉丁语 mutare“改变”，与 mutuus 同属一个原始印欧语词族，但意思是“可变的”，不是“被交换的”。

entries.definition: a change of form or genetic material. It is built on mutare 'to change', not on mutuus 'reciprocal'.
entries.definitionCN: 形态改变；基因突变。它建立在 mutare“改变”上，而不是 mutuus“相互的”上。

entries.definition: to travel regularly to work, or to reduce a punishment. It comes from Latin commutare 'to exchange, change', com- plus mutare.
entries.definitionCN: 通勤；减刑。它来自拉丁语 commutare“交换、改变”，由 com- 加 mutare 构成。

entries.definition: given or done by each side to the other. It is the strict term for the exchange sense, while mutual also covers shared possession.
entries.definitionCN: 相互给予或做出的。它是“交换”义的严格说法，而 mutual 还覆盖“共同拥有”。

entries.definition: belonging to or shared by several. It states joint possession without any idea of giving and receiving.
entries.definitionCN: 共有的；共同使用的。它只说明共同拥有，不含给予与接受的意思。

entries.definition: done or shared by two or more parties acting together, as in a joint statement.
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同做出或共享的，如 joint statement（联合声明）。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin stem mut-, the mutare family of mutable and mutation, and the documented history of mutual friend, mutual fund and MAD.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁词干 mut-、mutable 与 mutation 所属的 mutare 词族，以及 mutual friend、mutual fund、MAD 有据可查的历史。

normal.en: Picture an exchange: one hand gives a key, the other hand gives a key back. That is the original sense, 'reciprocally given and received'.
normal.cn: 想象一次交换：一只手递出钥匙，另一只手也递回钥匙。这就是本义“相互给予并接受”。

normal.en: Mutable, mutation and commute all carry Latin mutare 'to change'; mutual carries the same stem for an exchange of things or feelings.
normal.cn: mutable、mutation、commute 都带拉丁语 mutare“改变”；mutual 用同一词干表示物品或情感的交换。

normal.en: A mutual friend is a person both parties know, which is why critics call the phrase a loose use of 'common'.
normal.cn: a mutual friend 是两方都认识的人，正因如此，批评者说这个短语是对 common 的宽松误用。

normal.en: A mutual fund pools money, and mutual insurance pools risk: both are modern institutions built on shared ownership.
normal.cn: mutual fund 汇集资金，mutual insurance 汇集风险：两者都是建立在共同所有权上的现代制度。

normal.en: The standard frames are mutual respect, mutual understanding, mutual benefit and mutual agreement.
normal.cn: 标准搭配是 mutual respect、mutual understanding、mutual benefit 与 mutual agreement。

abstract.en: Two arrows drawn head to head: each direction needs the other, and a single arrow would not be mutual.
abstract.cn: 画两支箭头对着彼此：每个方向都需要另一边，只画一支就不叫 mutual。

abstract.en: A two-pan balance with equal weights: nothing tips, because what is given on one side is returned on the other.
abstract.cn: 一架两盘天平，两边砝码相等：哪边都不下沉，因为一边给出的在另一边被回敬。

abstract.en: Take one partner away and the word loses its point: mutual always needs a second party in the picture.
abstract.cn: 拿走一方，这个词就失去意义：mutual 的画面里永远需要一个“另一方”。

examples.en: The two countries signed the treaty out of mutual interest, not friendship.
examples.cn: 两国签署这项条约是出于共同利益，而非友谊。

examples.en: Mutual respect kept the debate civil even when the disagreement was sharp.
examples.cn: 相互尊重让这场辩论即使分歧尖锐也保持文明。

examples.en: They were introduced by a mutual friend who knew both families.
examples.cn: 他们是由一位认识两家人的共同朋友引见的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谬球」——两人把同一个球互相抛来抛去，你抛给我、我抛给你 → mutual 相互的、彼此的

root: 源自拉丁语 mutuus“相互的、交换而成的”，可追溯至原始印欧语 *mei-(1)“改变、移动”，核心是双方交换，而非共同拥有。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of mutual all grow from one picture: two parties handing something to each other. From exchanged feeling it extends to shared possession, then to contracts, member-owned institutions, formal relations and finally to the deadly symmetry of MAD.
sensesIntro.cn: mutual 的十个义项都从同一幅画生长出来：两方把东西递给对方。从被交换的情感，它扩展到共同拥有，再扩展到契约、会员共有的机构、形式关系，最后到 MAD 那种致命的对称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands passing the same key to each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把同一把钥匙互相递过去。

branches.en: THE EXCHANGE CORE: reciprocal action and reciprocal feeling, the oldest and strictest sense.
branches.cn: 交换核心：相互的行为与相互的情感，最古老也最严格的义项。

branches.en: SHARED, NOT EXCHANGED: the disputed mutual friend and the wider 'common' sense.
branches.cn: 共享而非交换：备受争议的 mutual friend，以及更宽的“共同”义。

branches.en: BENEFIT AND CONTRACT: advantage that runs both ways, and promises that bind both sides.
branches.cn: 利益与契约：双向流动的好处，以及约束双方的承诺。

branches.en: POOLED OWNERSHIP: member-owned insurance and the mutual fund, where sharing becomes an institution.
branches.cn: 汇聚式所有权：会员共有的保险与共同基金，共享在此变成制度。

branches.en: FORMAL SYMMETRY: mutual entailment in logic and the mutual destruction of the nuclear standoff.
branches.cn: 形式对称：逻辑中的相互蕴含，以及核对峙中的相互摧毁。

intro.en: Mutual is Latin mutuus plus the adjective suffix -al. English then builds mutually, mutuality, mutualism, mutualist, mutualize and mutualization, while the bare stem mut- lives on in mutation, mutable and commute.
intro.cn: mutual 是拉丁语 mutuus 加形容词后缀 -al。英语随后构造出 mutually、mutuality、mutualism、mutualist、mutualize 与 mutualization，而光秃的词干 mut- 仍活在 mutation、mutable、commute 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutuus 'reciprocal, done in exchange' is the direct source; the same stem gives mutare 'to change' and commutare 'to exchange'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus“相互的、交换而成的”是直接来源；同一词干还给出 mutare“改变”与 commutare“交换”。

items.meaningCN: 相互的；双方共享的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The agreement rests on mutual trust.
items.exampleCN: 这项协议建立在相互信任之上。

items.meaning: in a reciprocal way, each toward the other
items.meaningCN: 相互地；彼此地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two plans are mutually exclusive.

items.meaningCN: 相互性；共同性（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The contract depends on the mutuality of the promises.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同依赖于承诺的相互性。

items.meaning: a system of mutual dependence, or a symbiotic partnership
items.meaningCN: 互助主义；互利共生（-ism 构成体系名词）
items.example: Certain ants and plants live in mutualism.
items.exampleCN: 某些蚂蚁与植物处于互利共生关系。

items.meaning: a supporter of mutualism, or an organism in a mutual partnership
items.meaningCN: 互助主义者；互利共生的一方（-ist 构成人或形容词）
items.example: The coral and its algae are mutualists.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚与它的藻类是互利共生的一方。

items.meaning: to convert an enterprise into member ownership
items.meaningCN: 使共有；转为互助制（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The society voted to mutualize the savings bank.
items.exampleCN: 该协会投票决定把储蓄银行转为互助制。

items.meaningCN: 共有化；互助化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Mutualization changed how the insurer was governed.
items.exampleCN: 互助化改变了这家保险公司的治理方式。

items.meaning: a change of form or genetic material
items.example: The mutation gave the moths a darker wing.
items.exampleCN: 这次突变让蛾子的翅膀变深了。

items.meaningCN: 易变的；可改变的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: Language is mutable, and slang changes fastest.
items.exampleCN: 语言是可变的，而俚语变化最快。

items.meaning: to travel regularly, or to exchange one penalty for another
items.meaningCN: 通勤；减刑（com-“共同、交换”+ mut-“改变”）
items.example: She commutes by train every morning.
items.exampleCN: 她每天早上乘火车通勤。

definition_zh: 神秘的；难以解释的；讳莫如深的
definition_en: strange and difficult to explain; having a hidden or supernatural quality; deliberately keeping things unclear
core_image: 一扇只开一条缝的门，缝里透出一点看不清的光
scene: 村口的老宅多年无人居住，夜里楼上的窗子却总亮着。The old house keeps a mysterious light burning in its upper window.
sceneCN: 这里是「神秘的、难以解释的」（第 1 个义项：来路不明、说不清楚）；句意为那座老宅楼上窗里始终亮着一盏莫名的灯。图中可辨识物件：老宅、亮着的窗、夜色。

pos.zh: 神秘的；难以解释的；讳莫如深的

derivatives.zh: 由 mysterious 加 -ly 构成，义为「神秘地」
由 mysterious 加 -ness 构成，义为「神秘性」
与 mysterious 同出希腊语词根，义为「谜；神秘事物」

senses.title: Strange and hard to explain
senses.definition: difficult to understand or explain because the facts are hidden
senses.definitionCN: 因事实被遮蔽而难以理解或解释
senses.example: The old house keeps a mysterious light burning in its upper window.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老宅楼上窗里始终亮着一盏莫名的灯。
senses.why: Greek myein meant to close the lips or the eyes, so the family of words starts from what is shut away from view and only later describes how such a thing feels.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 myein 意为闭口或闭眼，因此这一族词的起点是「被关在视线之外的东西」，之后才用来形容这种东西给人的感觉。

senses.title: Touching on hidden or supernatural power
senses.titleCN: 带有神秘力量的；玄秘的
senses.definition: having a quality that seems to come from a hidden or supernatural source
senses.definitionCN: 带有似乎来自隐秘或超自然来源的性质
senses.example: The valley was said to hold mysterious forces that spoiled milk overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 据说那条山谷里有神秘的力量，能让牛奶一夜之间变坏。
senses.why: The word first named secret religious rites open only to the initiated; that closed door of ritual left it with a permanent air of the beyond.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指名只有入会者才能参加的秘仪；仪式那扇关着的门，让它永久带上了一层超验的气息。

senses.title: Deliberately unclear about something
senses.titleCN: 讳莫如深的；故意不说清
senses.definition: choosing to keep one's actions or intentions vague on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意把自己的行为或意图说得含糊
senses.example: She was mysterious about where the money had come from.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这笔钱的来路讳莫如深。
senses.why: Anyone who refuses to explain looks, from outside, exactly like a thing that cannot be explained, so the adjective moves from the unknown object to the person hiding it.
senses.whyCN: 一个人拒绝解释，从外面看就和一件无法解释的东西一模一样，于是这个形容词从被未知的对象转到了藏起它的人身上。

intro.en: Mysterious comes through French from Latin, where the noun had already travelled from Greek rites closed to outsiders.
intro.cn: mysterious 经法语来自拉丁语，而拉丁语中那个名词早已从「不许外人参与的希腊仪式」一路传来。

items.en: The verb myein meant to close, especially the eyes or the lips, and it gave the family its sense of shutting away.
items.cn: 动词 myein 意为闭合，尤指闭眼或闭嘴，为这一族词提供了「关起来、不示人」的意思。

items.en: A mysterion was a secret rite or doctrine revealed only to those admitted to it.
items.cn: mysterion 指只向获准入会者揭示的秘密仪式或教义。

items.en: Latin took the word as mysterium, keeping both the ritual sense and the broader sense of a secret.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词写作 mysterium，既保留仪式义，也泛指秘密。

items.en: French formed the adjective mysterieux from the same stem, and it carried the sense of something unexplained rather than something sacred.
items.cn: 法语用同一词干造出形容词 mysterieux，词义已偏向「说不清的事」，不再限于神圣之事。

items.en: English adopted the French adjective, respelled it with ous, and extended it to people who refuse to explain themselves.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语形容词，改写成带 ous 的形式，并把词义扩展到「不肯解释自己的人」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun, the adverb and other words on the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what cannot be explained.
note.cn: 形近组收同出希腊词根的名词、副词及其他同族词；近义组收表示「无法解释」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for something unexplained or kept secret.
entries.definitionCN: 表示无法解释或被人保密之事的名称。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a way that cannot be explained.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「神秘地、莫名其妙地」。

entries.definition: The quality of being strange and unexplained.
entries.definitionCN: 神秘、难以解释的性质。

entries.definition: To puzzle someone completely, from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 使人完全困惑，同出这一词干。

entries.definition: A person who seeks direct union with the divine.
entries.definitionCN: 追求与神直接合一的人；神秘的。

entries.definition: Unusual and hard to account for, but without the hint of hidden meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常、难以说明，但没有「背后另有隐情」的暗示。

entries.definition: Hard to understand because the pieces do not fit.
entries.definitionCN: 因线索拼不起来而令人费解。

entries.definition: Deliberately or naturally hard to read, like a riddle.
entries.definitionCN: 像谜语一样难以看透，可指有意为之。

entries.definition: Simply not yet accounted for, without any aura.
entries.definitionCN: 只是尚未得到解释，不带神秘气氛。

normalIntro.en: The word is the adjective of a Greek noun for closed rites, and its relatives still circle around secrets.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语中表示秘仪的名词的形容词形式，它的同族词至今仍围绕「秘密」打转。

normal.en: Greek myein meant to close the eyes or lips, so mysterious begins with the image of a mouth kept shut.
normal.cn: 希腊语 myein 意为闭上眼或闭上嘴，所以 mysterious 的起点是一张闭紧的嘴。

normal.en: Mystery is the noun and mysterious the adjective; adding ous turns a secret into a quality.
normal.cn: mystery 是名词，mysterious 是形容词；加上 ous，就把一个秘密变成了一种性质。

normal.en: The ending is said quickly as -əs, which is why the last syllable almost disappears in speech.
normal.cn: 词尾读得很轻，接近 -əs，所以最后一个音节在口语里几乎听不见。

normal.en: Mystify is the verb of the same family: to make someone feel they are facing a closed door.
normal.cn: mystify 是同一族的动词：让人觉得自己面对的是一扇关着的门。

normal.en: Mysterious circumstances and a mysterious smile both keep the facts just out of reach.
normal.cn: mysterious circumstances 与 a mysterious smile 都让事实停在伸手够不到的地方。

abstract.en: A door left ajar is more disturbing than a door locked tight, because the gap promises something behind it.
abstract.cn: 虚掩的门比紧锁的门更让人不安，因为那道缝许诺了门后有东西。

abstract.en: Every closed rite and every unopened letter teaches the same lesson about hidden knowledge.
abstract.cn: 每一场闭门仪式、每一封未拆的信，都在讲同一件关于隐秘知识的事。

abstract.en: A word that began with shut lips ends by describing the face of someone who will not answer.
abstract.cn: 一个从「闭紧嘴唇」开始的词，最后用来形容一张不肯回答的脸。

examples.en: A mysterious figure was seen near the gate last night.
examples.cn: 昨夜有人在门附近看见一个神秘的身影。

examples.en: The case remains mysterious after thirty years.
examples.cn: 三十年后这桩案子依然扑朔迷离。

examples.en: He gave a mysterious smile and changed the subject.
examples.cn: 他神秘地笑了笑，换了话题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯特瑞斯」——把秘密密起来，脸上就带出神秘；mysterious 就是神秘的。

root: 希腊语 myein（闭口、闭眼）构成 mysterion（秘仪），经拉丁语 mysterium 与法语 mysterieux 进入英语；一般认为词根与「闭合」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what is shut away from view; the senses spread from unexplained events to sacred hidden power and to people who hide their own reasons.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被关在视线之外」；义项从无法解释的事件，扩展到隐秘的神圣力量，再转到有意藏起自己理由的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opened only a crack, with a light inside that cannot be made out.
core.cn: 核心意象：只开一道缝的门，里面有看不清的光。

branches.en: a lamp left burning in an empty house
branches.cn: 空屋里一直亮着的灯

branches.en: a footprint that stops halfway across a room
branches.cn: 走到房间中间就断掉的脚印

branches.en: a rite held behind a curtain
branches.cn: 帘子后面举行的仪式

branches.en: milk souring overnight in a valley
branches.cn: 山谷里一夜变坏的牛奶

branches.en: an answer that slides away from the question
branches.cn: 绕开问题的回答

intro.en: The word is built from a Greek verb of closing, its noun of secret rites, a Latin borrowing, and an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语表「闭合」的动词、其表示秘仪的名词、拉丁语的借形，以及一个英语形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek noun as mysterium and formed mysticus from the same root, and both stand behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语名词借作 mysterium，又用同一词根造出 mysticus，两者都支撑着英语这一族词。
